| | Friend, Southern Minnesota landed on a list this week.A Washington, D.C. group called _Swing Left_ released a map of House seats they want to take from Republicans. Ours is on it as a top tier race, filed under "must-flip." **There are only twenty-nine such districts nationwide, and we're one of them.** So there's now an out-of-state PAC raising money off this district and signing up volunteers to come knock doors here. It’s not because anybody there knows what a bushel of corn is going for, or what folks are paying to keep the lights on. They need the seat. That's the whole reason.They're not the first, either. The DCCC put this race on its target list back in February. _Swing Left_ is just the newest socialist group attacking us.I've never treated this seat like it was mine to keep. I've got neighbors here standing with me, not left wing backers in New York and California like my opponent.

| | | **What counts as a _suspended voter_?** In Texas, it means that the voter’s county doesn’t know their address or thinks they’ve moved. It doesn’t necessarily stop people from voting in November’s midterm elections, but it does make the process of voting much more difficult. If a voter shows up on Election Day and their registration is suspended, they have to fill out a “ _statement of residence_ ” form, and if they’ve moved to a new county, they’ll either be required to vote in their old one or **be given a provisional ballot** , according to _The Dallas Morning News_. Just to be clear: **The rates of rejection on provisional ballots are substantially higher than mail-in ballots**. They are easier to question, easier to challenge and get thrown out, which is why we're trying to reach every eligible voter we can to have their registration verified to be valid for the upcoming election. There should be no doubt about how scared opponents of voting rights are if they're suddenly willing to go to these new extremes to pick and choose whose vote gets to count in the midterms. "We know six percent doesn't seem like a lot, but 1.2 million does. And elections are routinely decided by less than six percentage points. This is especially critical when Texas's upcoming Senate race is one of the most-watched and forecast as one of the tightest elections this November.The suspended registrations span the whole state, but also some of Texas’s largest counties, including Dallas County, where more than 129,000 voters are suspended; 56,000 voters in both Collin and Denton counties; and over 73,000 voters in Tarrant County. **Boysko Bulletin: Voting Starts Soon for Congressional Races and the 3 Constitutional Amendments
**
---
Dear Peter, I hope that you have enjoyed a lovely summer and that all students, educators, and parents are getting back in the swing of the new school year! It’s certainly been a busy summer for me and my team.

This November, we have the midterm elections for all Congressional seats. In the Town of Herndon, we have town council elections. And this year, all Virginia voters will have three Constitutional Amendments for consideration. I ask that you inform yourself with accurate information. I’ve provided ways that you can get involved below.

On the Constitutional Amendments, I will go into more detail further down in the newsletter but to sum it up succinctly, I urge you to vote yes if you agree that we should have:
* Freedom to decide for yourself about reproductive health with the advice and care from your doctor - not politicians;
* Freedom to marry the person you love without government interference;
* Freedom to vote and to be treated as a full-fledged citizen with the same rights and responsibilities as other Virginians after completing your incarceration when you return to the community.

Please join me for a Roundtable with Delegate Keys-Gamarra and Supervisor Alcorn, at the Reston Community Center at Lake Anne on September 14, at 6:30 pm. Please fill out this form in advance: [https://forms.gle/67P192emRPmPzcxd8](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138462280/644131539/1399327204?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNGIyNjE0ZjEtMmRhNy1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=ZZGFrG6LfKvUPBmqeA96JXypveDQArejZhxde_n_mLM=&emci=803cf210-4a97-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=4b2614f1-2da7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=22486556). **Legislative Updates** My 2027 Session Legislative Slate is off to a great start. I have requested drafts for 9 bills - tackling criminal justice reform, support for teachers, employment discrimination, healthcare access, and housing affordability. My schedule is filled with meetings with advocates and other stakeholders.. Our bill limit will be 15 bills plus an additional 5 if we requested the drafts by August 31 which I did. Once my legislation is drafted and changes made, I will file it and you will find the bills on [lis.virginia.gov](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138462282/644131541/303244636?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNGIyNjE0ZjEtMmRhNy1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=ZZGFrG6LfKvUPBmqeA96JXypveDQArejZhxde_n_mLM=&emci=803cf210-4a97-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=4b2614f1-2da7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=22486556) \- this is [my page](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138462283/644131542/-124516961?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNGIyNjE0ZjEtMmRhNy1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=ZZGFrG6LfKvUPBmqeA96JXypveDQArejZhxde_n_mLM=&emci=803cf210-4a97-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=4b2614f1-2da7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=22486556). I also have the opportunity to recognize members of our community for their accomplishments - please let me know if there is someone you would like to receive a commendation or memorial resolution. To submit ideas for legislation, please email senatorboysko@senate.virginia.gov. **Continue the Fight Against Tysons Casino Legislation** Governor Spanberger vetoed the 2026 Session casino legislation,****[SB 756](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138462284/644131543/-1821246626?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNGIyNjE0ZjEtMmRhNy1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=ZZGFrG6LfKvUPBmqeA96JXypveDQArejZhxde_n_mLM=&emci=803cf210-4a97-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=4b2614f1-2da7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=22486556), and the Senate sustained the veto by voting to pass the bill by for the day. In meetings with the Governor’s team, they mentioned the many emails you all sent. We have made it clear that our community does not want a casino, would not benefit from a casino financially, and in fact would be harmed by a casino. Despite the clear rejection of our community, sponsors of the legislation have vowed to introduce the bill again so we will continue the fight. All of you who oppose this proposal should stay engaged. By organizing, educating our neighbors, and reaching out to state leaders, we have made sure that our concerns were heard loud and clear and we will continue that work. You can sign up for updates, and take action, visit the [No Fairfax Casino coalition](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138462285/644131544/-833915805?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNGIyNjE0ZjEtMmRhNy1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=ZZGFrG6LfKvUPBmqeA96JXypveDQArejZhxde_n_mLM=&emci=803cf210-4a97-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=4b2614f1-2da7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=22486556). Together, we can continue building momentum and strengthen the No Tysons Casino movement. **Three Amendments to the Virginia Constitution on the November 3 Ballot** **Reproductive Freedom Amendment** The Reproductive Freedom amendment protects access to a broad range of reproductive health care and puts the power where it belongs—with Virginians, their families, and their doctors. No matter your faith or personal beliefs, these are decisions that should be made personally, not by the government. The amendment was crafted to follow the current laws in Virginia, to take the politics out of reproductive healthcare, and to protect the fundamental freedom to make these decisions for ourselves. You are probably aware that the US Supreme Court Dobbs decision removed the fundamental right to privacy regarding abortion, leaving it up to the states. The Constitutional Amendment will guarantee Virginians the fundamental right to reproductive freedom, including the ability to make and carry out decisions relating to one's own prenatal care, childbirth, postpartum care, contraception, abortion care, miscarriage management, and fertility care. The state would not be allowed to interfere with a person's right to make their own reproductive health choices, for example, by banning certain types of care (like abortion), or making it more difficult to access that care without a strong justification for why doing so would protect patients’ health and safety. The state would still be able to regulate abortion in the third trimester, including by restricting access to the procedure. But the Commonwealth would allow access to abortion, even in the third trimester, where it’s to protect the life or physical or mental health of the pregnant individual or when a fetus is not viable. Virginia would not be allowed to treat people differently from others on the basis of their identity when it comes to protecting or enforcing this basic right. Patients and doctors would be protected from being charged or jailed for accessing or providing reproductive healthcare. Virginia would not be allowed to punish or take action against someone for making their own reproductive healthcare decisions. Virginia also cannot punish someone who helps another person make these choices, as long as the person being helped agrees to it. Virginia would only get involved in someone’s reproductive healthcare choices if it’s necessary to protect or improve the person’s health. Any regulations the Commonwealth imposes on reproductive healthcare, like abortion, must follow trusted medical guidelines and research. The Commonwealth would not take away a person's right to make their own decisions about their body. This language prevents laws that create unnecessary obstacles to abortion care - like “Targeted Restrictions on Abortion Providers” or “TRAP” laws and laws like a 72-hour waiting period or biased counseling before an abortion. The General Assembly passed my legislation twice - once in the 2025 Session and once in the 2026 session. Constitutional amendments require passing the bill in two sessions with an intervening election. Delegate Herring passed identical resolutions. The referendum on the amendment will take place during the November 3 election and all registered voters can vote for or against the amendment. I am working with the [Virginians for Reproductive Freedom](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138462286/644131545/-494596654?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNGIyNjE0ZjEtMmRhNy1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=ZZGFrG6LfKvUPBmqeA96JXypveDQArejZhxde_n_mLM=&emci=803cf210-4a97-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=4b2614f1-2da7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=22486556) to encourage people to vote for the amendment. You can also volunteer with Planned Parenthood’s NOVA organizer, Rhea Simon, at [rsimon@ppav.org](mailto:rsimon@ppav.org). Now is the time to act—to secure reproductive freedom for generations to come. **I urge you to vote yes.** **Marriage Amendment** Question 2 would repeal Virginia's 2006 Marshall-Newman Amendment, a ban on marriage between same-sex couples that remains in our Virginia Constitution today, and replace it with an affirmative guarantee that the government must treat all marriages equally under the law. It would enshrine the freedom for adult couples to marry, as the current law in Virginia allows. [Virginians for Marriage Equality](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138462287/644131546/-2015354088?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNGIyNjE0ZjEtMmRhNy1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=ZZGFrG6LfKvUPBmqeA96JXypveDQArejZhxde_n_mLM=&emci=803cf210-4a97-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=4b2614f1-2da7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=22486556) is a coalition of Virginia families, couples, faith leaders, and advocacy organizations working to protect the freedom to marry in Virginia. Voters will see Question 2 on their general election ballot: Should the Constitution of Virginia be amended to (i) remove the ban on same-sex marriage; (ii) affirm that two adults may marry regardless of sex, gender, or race; (iii) require all legally valid marriages to be treated equally under the law? As Virginians, we value fairness, dignity, and equal rights. Every Virginian deserves the freedom to marry the person they love, free from government interference. This amendment is simple. It repeals Virginia’s ban on marriages between same-sex couples and ensures every Virginian can marry who they love, free from government interference. This amendment ensures all married couples are protected, no matter what happens at the federal level. Marriage is a fundamental right that provides legal protection, stability, and security. For over a decade, the law on marriage for same-sex couples has been clear, and people have made decisions – bought homes, raised families, built businesses, planned for life – based on it. Virginians shouldn’t have to question whether this right might be taken away in the future. This amendment is about our values. As Virginians, we believe that regardless of who we love, we should be able to live, work, and make deeply personal decisions about our lives with dignity, respect, and equal rights and freedoms. That’s what this amendment is all about. This amendment repeals Virginia's ban on same-sex marriage so Virginians – not politicians – have the freedom to make decisions that are right for themselves. Who you marry is one of the most personal decisions a person can make; the government has no place in deeply personal decisions about love, marriage, and family. This amendment ensures the freedom to marry the person you love is a right enjoyed by every Virginian for generations to come. **I urge you to vote yes.** **Restoration of Rights Amendment** The third Constitutional Amendment that you will see on your ballot pertains to the restoration of rights for returning citizens after completion of their incarceration. It creates an explicit constitutional right to vote for every eligible Virginian, something Virginia’s Constitution does not currently guarantee. Protect against current and future attacks on voting rights by taking the right to vote out of politicians’ hands. Ensure a fair process that doesn’t rely on the whims of politicians by automatically restoring voting rights to Virginians with felony convictions once they have completed their sentences and returned to their communities. The amendment also protects people with disabilities from automatically losing their right to vote when put under a guardianship by empowering judges to decide case-by-case if that person understands the act of voting. Learn more at [https://www.varighttovote.org/about-us](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138462288/644131547/-146069721?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNGIyNjE0ZjEtMmRhNy1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=ZZGFrG6LfKvUPBmqeA96JXypveDQArejZhxde_n_mLM=&emci=803cf210-4a97-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=4b2614f1-2da7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=22486556). **I urge you to vote yes.** **Herndon Town Council Election Update** The mayor and all members of the Herndon Town Council are on the ballot this November. If you are a town resident, living in Herndon 1, 2 or 3 precincts, [I urge you to do your research on all of the candidates.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138462289/644131575/-2108672901?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNGIyNjE0ZjEtMmRhNy1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=ZZGFrG6LfKvUPBmqeA96JXypveDQArejZhxde_n_mLM=&emci=803cf210-4a97-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=4b2614f1-2da7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=22486556) There will be a number of opportunities to meet and listen to the candidates. I am helping host an event for four promising new candidates in September.

**Opportunities** **Share Your Concerns About the Proposed NextEra - Dominion Merger** Many of you have written to me about the proposed Dominion and NextEra merger. I have been collecting information to better understand the impact of a merger and recently held a town hall with Delegate Shin. The Virginia State Corporation Commission (SCC) has the authority to approve or block the merger if it determines the deal does not benefit or if it harms Virginia ratepayers. clean_body: | | | | Boysko Bulletin: Voting Starts Soon for Congressional Races and the 3 Constitutional Amendments Dear Peter, I hope that you have enjoyed a lovely summer and that all students, educators, and parents are getting back in the swing of the new school year! It’s certainly been a busy summer for me and my team. This November, we have the midterm elections for all Congressional seats. In the Town of Herndon, we have town council elections. And this year, all Virginia voters will have three Constitutional Amendments for consideration. I ask that you inform yourself with accurate information. I’ve provided ways that you can get involved below. On the Constitutional Amendments, I will go into more detail further down in the newsletter but to sum it up succinctly, I urge you to vote yes if you agree that we should have: Freedom to decide for yourself about reproductive health with the advice and care from your doctor - not politicians; Freedom to marry the person you love without government interference; Freedom to vote and to be treated as a full-fledged citizen with the same rights and responsibilities as other Virginians after completing your incarceration when you return to the community. Please join me for a Roundtable with Delegate Keys-Gamarra and Supervisor Alcorn, at the Reston Community Center at Lake Anne on September 14, at 6:30 pm. Please fill out this form in advance: . Hope to see you there. Kindest regards, Jennifer B. You can sign up for updates, and take action, visit the . Together, we can continue building momentum and strengthen the No Tysons Casino movement. Three Amendments to the Virginia Constitution on the November 3 Ballot Reproductive Freedom Amendment The Reproductive Freedom amendment protects access to a broad range of reproductive health care and puts the power where it belongs—with Virginians, their families, and their doctors. No matter your faith or personal beliefs, these are decisions that should be made personally, not by the government. The amendment was crafted to follow the current laws in Virginia, to take the politics out of reproductive healthcare, and to protect the fundamental freedom to make these decisions for ourselves. You are probably aware that the US Supreme Court Dobbs decision removed the fundamental right to privacy regarding abortion, leaving it up to the states. The Constitutional Amendment will guarantee Virginians the fundamental right to reproductive freedom, including the ability to make and carry out decisions relating to one's own prenatal care, childbirth, postpartum care, contraception, abortion care, miscarriage management, and fertility care. The state would not be allowed to interfere with a person's right to make their own reproductive health choices, for example, by banning certain types of care (like abortion), or making it more difficult to access that care without a strong justification for why doing so would protect patients’ health and safety. The state would still be able to regulate abortion in the third trimester, including by restricting access to the procedure. But the Commonwealth would allow access to abortion, even in the third trimester, where it’s to protect the life or physical or mental health of the pregnant individual or when a fetus is not viable. Virginia would not be allowed to treat people differently from others on the basis of their identity when it comes to protecting or enforcing this basic right. Patients and doctors would be protected from being charged or jailed for accessing or providing reproductive healthcare. Virginia would not be allowed to punish or take action against someone for making their own reproductive healthcare decisions. Virginia also cannot punish someone who helps another person make these choices, as long as the person being helped agrees to it. Virginia would only get involved in someone’s reproductive healthcare choices if it’s necessary to protect or improve the person’s health. Any regulations the Commonwealth imposes on reproductive healthcare, like abortion, must follow trusted medical guidelines and research. The Commonwealth would not take away a person's right to make their own decisions about their body. This language prevents laws that create unnecessary obstacles to abortion care - like “Targeted Restrictions on Abortion Providers” or “TRAP” laws and laws like a 72-hour waiting period or biased counseling before an abortion. The General Assembly passed my legislation twice - once in the 2025 Session and once in the 2026 session. Constitutional amendments require passing the bill in two sessions with an intervening election. Delegate Herring passed identical resolutions. The referendum on the amendment will take place during the November 3 election and all registered voters can vote for or against the amendment. I am working with the to encourage people to vote for the amendment. You can also volunteer with Planned Parenthood’s NOVA organizer, Rhea Simon, at mailto:rsimon@ppav.org. Now is the time to act—to secure reproductive freedom for generations to come. I urge you to vote yes. Marriage Amendment Question 2 would repeal Virginia's 2006 Marshall-Newman Amendment, a ban on marriage between same-sex couples that remains in our Virginia Constitution today, and replace it with an affirmative guarantee that the government must treat all marriages equally under the law. It would enshrine the freedom for adult couples to marry, as the current law in Virginia allows. is a coalition of Virginia families, couples, faith leaders, and advocacy organizations working to protect the freedom to marry in Virginia. Voters will see Question 2 on their general election ballot: Should the Constitution of Virginia be amended to (i) remove the ban on same-sex marriage; (ii) affirm that two adults may marry regardless of sex, gender, or race; (iii) require all legally valid marriages to be treated equally under the law? As Virginians, we value fairness, dignity, and equal rights. Every Virginian deserves the freedom to marry the person they love, free from government interference. This amendment is simple. It repeals Virginia’s ban on marriages between same-sex couples and ensures every Virginian can marry who they love, free from government interference. This amendment ensures all married couples are protected, no matter what happens at the federal level. Marriage is a fundamental right that provides legal protection, stability, and security. For over a decade, the law on marriage for same-sex couples has been clear, and people have made decisions – bought homes, raised families, built businesses, planned for life – based on it. Virginians shouldn’t have to question whether this right might be taken away in the future. This amendment is about our values. As Virginians, we believe that regardless of who we love, we should be able to live, work, and make deeply personal decisions about our lives with dignity, respect, and equal rights and freedoms. That’s what this amendment is all about. This amendment repeals Virginia's ban on same-sex marriage so Virginians – not politicians – have the freedom to make decisions that are right for themselves. Who you marry is one of the most personal decisions a person can make; the government has no place in deeply personal decisions about love, marriage, and family. This amendment ensures the freedom to marry the person you love is a right enjoyed by every Virginian for generations to come. I urge you to vote yes. Restoration of Rights Amendment The third Constitutional Amendment that you will see on your ballot pertains to the restoration of rights for returning citizens after completion of their incarceration. It creates an explicit constitutional right to vote for every eligible Virginian, something Virginia’s Constitution does not currently guarantee. Protect against current and future attacks on voting rights by taking the right to vote out of politicians’ hands. Ensure a fair process that doesn’t rely on the whims of politicians by automatically restoring voting rights to Virginians with felony convictions once they have completed their sentences and returned to their communities. The amendment also protects people with disabilities from automatically losing their right to vote when put under a guardianship by empowering judges to decide case-by-case if that person understands the act of voting. Learn more at . I urge you to vote yes. Herndon Town Council Election Update The mayor and all members of the Herndon Town Council are on the ballot this November. I have been collecting information to better understand the impact of a merger and recently held a town hall with Delegate Shin. The Virginia State Corporation Commission (SCC) has the authority to approve or block the merger if it determines the deal does not benefit or if it harms Virginia ratepayers. The SCC is in the process of conducting a robust examination of the proposal. Dominion Energy and NextEra Energy filed their official merger application with the SCC on July 15, 2026. Thousands of questions are expected to be asked to fully vet the public’s interest during the process. Dominion will be required to answer all of them. The SCC has assigned this proposed merger Case Number PUR-2026-00112 and the public comment period is taking place from July 21, 2026 to November 9, 2026. You can submit a public comment about this merger. I encourage you to use your voice to express your concerns. The full petition for the proposed merger can be found and I've highlighted information about public hearings you can attend below: Hearings for the receipt of testimony from public witnesses on the Joint Petition shall be convened telephonically on November 5, 2026, from 8:30 a.m. until 11:00 a.m.: November 9, 2026, from 4:00 p.m. until 7:00 p.m.; and November 10, 2026, from 4:00 p.m. until 7:00 p.m. Each witness will be allotted five minutes to provide testimony. This public witness hearing will be webcast at . On or before November 2, 2026, any person desiring to offer testimony as a public witness shall provide required contact information to the Commission. This information may be provided to the Commission: (i) by filling out a form on the Commission’s website at scc.virginia.gov/case-information/webcasting: or (ii) by calling (804)-371-9141. The evidentiary portion of the hearing on the Joint Petition shall be convened at 10 a.m. on November 17, 2026, in the Commission’s second floor courtroom located in the Tyler Building, 1300 East Main Street, Richmond, Virginia 23219, to receive the testimony and evidence of the Petitioners, any respondents, and Staff on the Joint Petition. I’ve also written to the SCC asking for public hearings in northern Virginia. I encourage you to testify, submit your concerns and to fully engage in the process. Additionally, Governor Spanberger recently announced that she plans to intervene in the merger, meaning that she “will formally request to be a party to the case”. By becoming a party to the case, the Governor will have the legal right to “engage, bring concerns forward, request detailed information about the proposed merger, and make clear that Virginians expect to see long-term, tangible benefits of any potential deal.” Do You Enjoy Writing? Men and women convicted of a federal crime serve their sentences in a federal prison. They are incarcerated in 122 prisons around the United States, from California to Florida to upstate New York. They feel very isolated since they are often incarcerated so far from home. To address their isolation, in November 2017, Interfaith Action for Human Rights (lAHR) kicked off a campaign to identify volunteers who will write to at least one person in prison once a month for a year. As of June 2026, over 300 people have volunteered to be pen pals with a person incarcerated in a federal prison or a Virginia State Prison. There are still over 150 people in prison who have requested a pen pal, with new requests coming in every week. We need more pen pals on the outside to meet the need on the inside. Martin is fighting for reliable, affordable power and a more reliable grid for communities across the country. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138462624/644141947/-272948131?refcode=AU_MTH_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20260902_PM1_V1_S2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS84OTA0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhOWUxYjY1ZS0zMGE3LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=kzBZK6d9OWXm44HuNOkk2mMk4KlpabMc1IlMH2FOuJw=&emci=a2e1b65e-30a7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=a9e1b65e-30a7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=252045)
---
Friend, America’s electricity demand is growing fast, driven in part by AI data centers, hyperscalers, and other massive new electricity users. That raises an important question: _Who should pay for the expensive grid upgrades needed to connect them?_ Martin believes the answer is clear: If a company creates the need for new infrastructure, that company should pay for it — **_not_ families and small businesses.** That’s the principle behind Martin’s GRID Savings Act. The legislation would require the largest new electricity users to take financial responsibility for the grid upgrades needed to serve them, while creating incentives for these companies to invest in major transmission projects. It would also increase transparency and help protect grid reliability. America needs a stronger grid to keep up with growing energy demand. But working families and small businesses shouldn’t be left footing the bill for infrastructure built primarily to serve the nation’s biggest energy users. Martin is fighting for sustainable, affordable power and a more reliable grid for communities across the country. **But he can’t do it alone.** [_**Will you add your name to our petition calling for big electricity users to pay their fair share of the grid upgrades they require?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138462625/644141948/790441620?refcode=AU_MTH_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20260902_PM1_V1_S2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS84OTA0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhOWUxYjY1ZS0zMGE3LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=kzBZK6d9OWXm44HuNOkk2mMk4KlpabMc1IlMH2FOuJw=&emci=a2e1b65e-30a7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=a9e1b65e-30a7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=252045) | [SIGN THE PETITION](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138462626/644141949/790441620?refcode=AU_MTH_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20260902_PM1_V1_S2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS84OTA0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhOWUxYjY1ZS0zMGE3LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=kzBZK6d9OWXm44HuNOkk2mMk4KlpabMc1IlMH2FOuJw=&emci=a2e1b65e-30a7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=a9e1b65e-30a7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=252045)

body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=8688%2E582294%2EMnw4XY ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=8688%2E582294%2EMnw4XY ]Chris Pappas for Senate

Here are
where things stand in New Hampshire with just nine weeks left in the
election:

FIRST: The GOP pledged to pour millions into New Hampshire to flip this
seat red – we’re being outspent 3:1 on TV ads.

THEN: New polls show my opponent John Sununu ahead in this race for the
first time this entire campaign – the avalanche of outside money is
working in Republicans’ favor.

It's hard to believe we're already in September!

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/n7qDMjSMpAv?e=1c5f08419c&c2id=9f711ebcee4618a2092828a4c98e410a)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |

### **September is here, the kids are back at school, and Election Day is just 62 days away. We’ve got big plans for the weeks ahead – lots of doors to knock and people to talk to ahead of November. But before I get too far ahead, I want to take a moment to tell you all about what I was up to last month. August was action-packed! I traveled all over the district, meeting with people from all walks of life. I had so many meaningful conversations and was able to connect with so many of you. It was a wonderful end to an unforgettable summer. I’m so grateful for your continued support on this journey – together, we’re going to get this done.**
---
| |
### Best, Eileen.

| | I spent a lot of time out on the Eastern Plains in August, and one thing that’s stood out to me as I’ve traveled around the district listening to people is how rural America has been left behind by politicians in both parties for far too long. I attended a **farmers roundtable in Lamar** at the beginning of the month and heard about how the price of fuel and fertilizer has skyrocketed as a result of the Iran War, meaning that farmers are left to make tough decisions when it comes to purchasing diesel and fertilizing their fields. Some are choosing not to fertilize their land at all. It is striking to me that although most of our food is grown in rural America, Congress has not been able to pass a full Farm Bill in almost 8 years. We have to do better for our farmers, ranchers, and producers.
This also became clear to me when I met with the **Colorado Livestock Association** shortly after the Administration’s announcement that they were going to import over 660 million pounds of beef, and we discussed the fact that this plan will create more uncertainty for ranchers in an already unstable market and hurt growth for the United States cattle herd. It’s important to engage directly with the experts when it comes to making policy decisions, which is why I’ve been meeting with as many stakeholder groups in the district as possible.
Another area I’ve been working to build coalitions in is rural health care. I’m proud to say that as of this month, **I have visited every rural hospital in Colorado’s 4th District.** I’ve heard all about the challenges these hospitals are facing – the “death by a thousand cuts” to Medicaid, unfair pricing and reimbursement from insurance companies, and insufficient funding, to name a few. Independent rural hospitals are the backbone of their communities. Many of them are among the top three employers in their counties, and they provide essential services to every person that walks through their doors. They’ve been underserved by their government for too long. To me, this isn’t the end of my tour of these rural hospitals – this is the beginning of a working relationship, and I intend to start a Rural Health Advisory Council when I’m elected to ensure that the legislation I’m writing and voting in Congress will support these hospitals.
As we’ve been getting nearer to the election, I’ve been working to get my message as far across the district as possible, and to that end I was thrilled to be a guest on a number of podcasts and radio shows this month! I enjoyed talking with Jeff and Bill, hosts of **The Jeff and Bill Show on 710 KNUS** about all kinds of things, from the Iran War to working on common-sense, bipartisan legislation. And I had a lovely time talking with **Emily Suyat** on her podcast, **Red County Blue State,** about what it means to serve your country and your district. But some of the most meaningful conversations were on **Meidas Defense** and **MS Now,** talking about the conditions of sailors aboard the _USS Abraham Lincoln_ and the total lack of leadership that has brought us here. Our servicemembers and their families deserve leaders who understand the consequence and weight of what is being asked of them, and I will never stop fighting to support them.
It was also a great honor to speak at the **Colorado Water Congress** toward the end of August. I was inspired by the people I met and listened to there, and pledged to work with local and state governments and water groups, as well as colleagues on both sides of the aisle in Congress, to pass legislation that will shore up Colorado’s water infrastructure and build for the future.
And, I’ve had a blast attending canvass launches and starting to knock doors around the district! My campaign is planning to knock doors in every corner of the district, and the work is already well underway, thanks to my amazing team of organizers. I’m also excited to announce that **my campaign has opened an office in Loveland** to have a home base there. I’m looking forward to knocking thousands more doors in the coming weeks, and hope to see some of you out there!

I’m so grateful for your continued support on this journey – together, we’re going to get this done. | | Best, Eileen. | | | | | | | I spent a lot of time out on the Eastern Plains in August, and one thing that’s stood out to me as I’ve traveled around the district listening to people is how rural America has been left behind by politicians in both parties for far too long. I attended a farmers roundtable in Lamar at the beginning of the month and heard about how the price of fuel and fertilizer has skyrocketed as a result of the Iran War, meaning that farmers are left to make tough decisions when it comes to purchasing diesel and fertilizing their fields. Some are choosing not to fertilize their land at all. It is striking to me that although most of our food is grown in rural America, Congress has not been able to pass a full Farm Bill in almost 8 years. We have to do better for our farmers, ranchers, and producers. This also became clear to me when I met with the Colorado Livestock Association shortly after the Administration’s announcement that they were going to import over 660 million pounds of beef, and we discussed the fact that this plan will create more uncertainty for ranchers in an already unstable market and hurt growth for the United States cattle herd. It’s important to engage directly with the experts when it comes to making policy decisions, which is why I’ve been meeting with as many stakeholder groups in the district as possible. Another area I’ve been working to build coalitions in is rural health care. I’m proud to say that as of this month, I have visited every rural hospital in Colorado’s 4th District. I’ve heard all about the challenges these hospitals are facing – the “death by a thousand cuts” to Medicaid, unfair pricing and reimbursement from insurance companies, and insufficient funding, to name a few. Independent rural hospitals are the backbone of their communities. Many of them are among the top three employers in their counties, and they provide essential services to every person that walks through their doors. They’ve been underserved by their government for too long. To me, this isn’t the end of my tour of these rural hospitals – this is the beginning of a working relationship, and I intend to start a Rural Health Advisory Council when I’m elected to ensure that the legislation I’m writing and voting in Congress will support these hospitals. As we’ve been getting nearer to the election, I’ve been working to get my message as far across the district as possible, and to that end I was thrilled to be a guest on a number of podcasts and radio shows this month! I enjoyed talking with Jeff and Bill, hosts of The Jeff and Bill Show on 710 KNUS about all kinds of things, from the Iran War to working on common-sense, bipartisan legislation. And I had a lovely time talking with Emily Suyat on her podcast, Red County Blue State, about what it means to serve your country and your district. But some of the most meaningful conversations were on Meidas Defense and MS Now, talking about the conditions of sailors aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln and the total lack of leadership that has brought us here. Our servicemembers and their families deserve leaders who understand the consequence and weight of what is being asked of them, and I will never stop fighting to support them. It was also a great honor to speak at the Colorado Water Congress toward the end of August. I was inspired by the people I met and listened to there, and pledged to work with local and state governments and water groups, as well as colleagues on both sides of the aisle in Congress, to pass legislation that will shore up Colorado’s water infrastructure and build for the future. And, I’ve had a blast attending canvass launches and starting to knock doors around the district! My campaign is planning to knock doors in every corner of the district, and the work is already well underway, thanks to my amazing team of organizers. I’m also excited to announce that my campaign has opened an office in Loveland to have a home base there. I’m looking forward to knocking thousands more doors in the coming weeks, and hope to see some of you out there! | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Workers at the Cargill meatpacking plant in Fort Morgan reached a deal with a new five-year contract earlier this month, bringing an end to a three-month lockout. body:
You haven't just cheered me on from the sidelines; you’ve put on your boots and walked right alongside me.

| [](https://trk.emails.susancollinsformaine._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTQ1JmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDkwM19GRi1XUS4xMTAxMTdfdDIwMTAzNTEtMTE0MiZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA5MDNfRkYtV1EuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDEwMzUxLTExNDIifQ/-KbNxpYLiDJegryKTpLLZQ)
---
Dear Peter, I am writing this note not just as your Senator, but as a girl from Caribou who is continuously awed by the heart of this state. Thank you for opening your doors to me, for sharing your stories, and for pouring your time, energy, and hope into this work.You haven't just cheered me on from the sidelines, you’ve put on your boots and walked right alongside me. You’ve handed out signs, knocked on doors, and reminded me every single day why we fight so hard to find common ground. When people ask me where I find the strength to navigate the tough votes and the long days, the answer is simple: I look to you, Peter. I think of the Maine spirit: resilient, practical, deeply kind, and fiercely independent. Everything we have built, every policy we have crafted to protect our families, our lobstermen, our seniors, and our future, bears your fingerprints.**Thank you for believing in the power of conversation over conflict. Thank you for trusting me with your voices. And above all, thank you for giving me the greatest privilege of my life: bringing the character of Maine to the floor of the United States Senate.** We still have more trails to clear and more work to do, but today, I just want to pause and say how deeply, profoundly grateful I am to have you in my corner.
---

| MAGA has declared war against free and fair elections.
For months, Defend Our Courts has warned that MAGA was plotting to rig upcoming elections by any means possible. What Bannon revealed confirms exactly the type of extreme measures that we feared: they are preparing to use federal force to interfere with voting itself.
MAGA knows it is headed for major losses if elections remain free and fair. Instead of changing course, it is choosing coercion. Instead of persuasion, it is choosing fear.
And it’s important to be clear about how this works.
In most states, the presence of law enforcement at polling places is tightly regulated—or prohibited entirely—by state law. The authority to stop voter intimidation does not come from Washington. It comes from state courts, and ultimately from state Supreme Courts.
That is why MAGA’s long-term strategy has focused on capturing those courts. This is not new. This is the next phase.
Defend Our Courts helped lead the successful defense of the Pennsylvania Supreme Court—a critical firewall in the most important swing state in the country. That victory wasn’t symbolic. It protected the court that would have final say over election disputes in 2026 and beyond.
Now MAGA is escalating nationwide.
In 2026, state Supreme Court elections will take place in Michigan, Wisconsin, and Georgia—the very states where voter intimidation would be most consequential, and where courts will be called on to intervene if MAGA follows through on its threats.
This is why Defend Our Courts exists. We saw what was coming early. We rallied over 100 thousand Democrats to support our cause and built a winning model in Pennsylvania.
Now we are taking our winning formula national. With Democrats stretched thin by House and Senate races, defending democracy in the courts will not happen unless we do it.

## Iran Hits US Bases as War Reignites
The war with Iran [ramped back up](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2unTAQBeDVmM7IP2C4hYs0dC9tSmTwcJnEYOQZQHf3EW8Lr57R0fnOn6_xK2DC_f07bOB5yeMONyVghjJiCfuKTCdxyfkgzeXcjjnjaJRxUr2ksmOYGS8Ym1BFvwAYsBV43fV9Y5Uyqlr9HNpOt22rtFFTtNFpF5wOYNopxjbaCv2Tp17KaqVc29cuQuiMm5bu1dheR9EoiMi51H8z7rzCkj75glLPeauSX5kPEvaXMIMww33f9TzR43juwgwJL5DnEQMDCTOcJB-ZvEOR3yIZkTYkApIRj5S3MH8kw_o8UfiQvCFG3N9yRZa4S-KC_0CYoSo-HjemhOQ60aj3FjB9l-Ifbnl58z8AAP__M2uMyw) on Wednesday with the heaviest exchange since July. U.S. strikes hit Revolutionary Guard targets Tuesday night, and Iran answered with missiles and drones at bases hosting American troops in Jordan, Kuwait, and Bahrain. No U.S. casualties were reported. Iranian officials [accused Washington](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGupDAQRE9jMlDTZmwIHGxCNptuiAxuht41GNk9g_b2X_wr_KikCqr03p_n9PQc-Xj99js5WdN00FUiiVCeOPtjYynvIjmls7SS3_u5JJ4Q0NQw1KAnvwh_aOp8FdxKhKQrcq3t-04DIFSbMwHmhwbUpm9xRgBtqYPeGEBryNuK3b0HA-gWwDz6xgTyFs282qHTfRtUBxRYUm7-Jj5kozX-Tx_KzZL2KrpN5CxK_1I4Khyv62qWeWkWr3C8ae4u5RgUjjdRLbTd8T5YKNRFvFCpi2T-R6UeGqtxAA1VduG8OEYuxqoOXrvn-H0oP_T0cfgVAAD__wfAfBE) of striking a wedding party in southern Iran, killing four people. A U.S. military spokesman said the reports came from Iranian state media, are being looked into, and that the U.S. never targets civilians. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, traded near $95 a barrel on Wednesday, about 40% higher than a year ago. Stocks fell in Asia and Europe. President Trump warned that if Iran keeps retaliating, "they'll be no longer." He also asked on Truth Social whether the strait should be renamed the "TRUMP STRAIT." [See the post here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFqxDAQBNCvsbs7VitZsgoVgeDuUgVSGllenxVky0h7d-Tvg_MLaWfgwczXbbz5mOJ-__AbOV7yuNOrJmKmMsbi9zVyfVQuOR9VcHlsR8hxREB9AXsBOfrA8Umj8u3sFiIk2ZITpu-VBEBoV-fDNEEApSBQkDZ0PVmFGlQI0lg_tdGdHliQAkB3_VXP5A3qaTFWyV7MjQKaI-dy_c5x55WW9JOfVK4hb21yK_NRG_nW4NDgwOXBa80h-nT2Z6igkE_vefdp_jw3NDgcuXJtcBDCIKCQKE1nut5K3RY3H6-YUqzaNArum49_VMv_fOjp8DcAAP__8_t5mw).
## Germany Accuses Russia in Failed Leipzig Attack
Germany [formally blamed Russia](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSozAQRL8GMrnGAoMIFFzibC-9kBrQyJ49oaFGwuz-_ZXvFzbtrurq9_58zB_IifPjN27ka5Q501kS1Uo6s2J-ci1HqSqyl2vVY9tX4dmCHQxMBroZ18ovmntsg49ElrqW_HV0ru8ALLRP38clgoPlRi4ixNu0LNOKsK7O2ek2Li379x5M0F0Bhpu7DIFwtMMSx6nv3DU0PVDgKnr5FM71STF9y4v0ssrWJv-sdS9N96ux98bez_O8RPl6c7z7dyKaQmPvD9IN87dZEm5UjB6lMBr62pMUfpFJGCiboJLJRDlyMJlQzfFXkTNjNivqQ8yeMFMxG36KGmTdRWurPuwnp8RlGJseHhty-n-v_tDqy9t_AQAA__8ba5Ig) Tuesday for a failed drone attack on Leipzig's airport, citing forensic evidence and intelligence findings. Until this week, Berlin had said only that "foreign powers" may have been involved. A drone carrying explosives that failed to detonate was found on Aug. 4 beside a Ukrainian cargo plane that [shuttles ammunition](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL3SnDAMRZ_GdN7Rmr-lcJGGbtOmZGQQoMTYHlsLSZ4-Q17ha1SdObr3_nhPb2TPYfuOB1lZ4xToKp5EKE-cMews5VMkx5jKU_LnSHPkyYDpNAwa6gln4ZOmBqvFrkSG6orss3-9mhrAQLXbFmfnZsDWAXY99QO1Td-5GgZoWzdQxfb2wQD1E6BrX49uIexN59Z-aOrXc1EN0MIS8-Nn5CA7rf5PPCk_5nhU3u4iqaj6mzKjMuN1XY-FVgqF7i43o8y4-ejQKzPSJ8dEyoz3T2VGGO5jboTygUFvtzkcFEQ7jwcVnT-lMOo1Zu2J01_eNHJOMYtecgykUQTnX_pi2TX9Tj4WPqkoM1bZLuli77l0vWpgO5D9_9TyxbFPa_4FAAD__7-eluU) out of Leipzig. A bomb squad defused it, and similar drones turned up near the airport in the weeks after. Berlin answered by [closing Russia's last consulate](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1urDAQRp_GdCAz_JnCxW3o9rYpkbEHmMhgyx4WbZ4-2hR5gdSf9Omc8_GYH4Y8ndt_c6DmNcwn3tkjM6aZkjl34nxlTiHEXHO6jmgDzSChL-VYymY2lumJc2sKp1dEwKZAXQ9KtY2UIItd20XZBeq1HcE4M6rOteis7Y0bO4TFFaTff3KUTS1l36mqd2gG6Jd1GNtG1U60Eh1xSNVnoJN3XP0rPDFVNhyF1ztzzKL5J2ASMN33XWVOFDG_dwET72gYUxYw4ZVCRAHTrwEImDZMhzlfZbpyJlO6FE7MpUeKX7SVAAOorh6qnQ9fJO3iTd5T7gfRyu0w5H84-I_5nhq-AwAA__-h2YWb) in the country, shutting a cultural center suspected of spying, and tightening entry rules for Russian citizens. The EU and NATO vowed to [step up pressure](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD3O4zAMRE8jdwwY2vFP4WIbd9-2Wxq0TCdcyJIh0Qly-0Vyhe0H82ben5_5hzVovP_mXUbb0hzlVYKYSZ41c3yolbNYTukoV8vnfvikMyG1gANgPbM3fcrccLWOmwhJXcl47fq-qREJq8e4CHm_DNgPdFtFCBfeuuXmG18TIw2Vjp8-HLC-Ira3_tKuwh21y9YNTd1fV9egrGopX_4mjfaQLbzTU_LFp70K48PsKK7-5WhyNEU2TZFDEX9mtffn0CfoaPpgHE04OJrkBI4rRLYEz_QCS1BMDjgPOLKUcmaBFCGfpSgDbyYZorxAiufwRYBGuEveOb4dTVUe1-OlIWhpO9fgfWcN34H2n16fI_0LAAD__64bkEc) on Moscow, with EU chief Ursula von der Leyen calling Leipzig "a new escalation" on European Union soil. President Putin condemned Germany's response as a serious mistake.
## US Mint Starts Selling Trump $1 Coins
The U.S. Mint [began selling](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL-OtCAUxZ8GOwxcHNSC4mvs5mu3NAiX8W5QDDCaffuN8wrbneQk58_v6zk_LUXaX__thqaGNO94lYi1Yp4p232lWt6l5pSOImt-b4dLNIMAzcXIhZqtq3Ti3NnGm4AIqBo0sh-GTgkBollNgDEMOqheOg1eukU-1OKVBHyIARfXkLnzxCiUFEI_hlZ7tD3oJfRjpwbpWSfQU025_U601xVD_Ekn5talrYlmrfUoTP1jMDGYrutq3VLuH7fPYLolg-mznkvuU4w2c5doL_xd-EZ75cVGZDA12fjjohip6J514rVZip-a-kc6p4HfAAAA__8ClXrk) $1 coins stamped with President Trump's likeness Wednesday to mark the nation's 250th anniversary. The gold-colored dollars, which contain no actual gold, sell in rolls of 25 for $61 and bags of 100 for $154.50. Trump's portrait appears beneath "Liberty," with "1776 ~ 2026" below and the presidential eagle on the back. [See the coin here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0N2qnDAUxfGn0bvINvH4cZGLAz0DLVhoz0AvJZNsdQ8xsclW6duXziv0BRbr9_81TqMhT2H5bjbUPMcp4JU9MmOaKJmwEucjc4pxzzWnY9ttpEmCbAUMAtRkLNOJU2NKp2dEiapEXXd93ygACeWq33o5oFKNbR_QQtODG2oD1sAsneqsKUn_24MBVA3QvvVV69B0sn3M3dCovnZFA-iIY6qekQKvOPs_8cRU2biVXq_Mey7UeyFvhbxd11UdeaPA1RLPQt4ybvT7oGAxMIZAxos9YSaHgYWLwXgnnuJlEy9YLWykIFL0PouHWbIY3z_vHz-nz4_x648v3-7Vypsvk3b7Rd5TbruigWUz5F-P-D9Dnlr-DQAA__--Q4nw). The Mint randomly mixed in 250,000 coins struck on July 4 bearing a special holiday mark. Federal law generally bars living presidents from appearing on U.S. currency. Officials leaned on an anniversary exception, and Trump called the idea "very unusual" but said he was "honored by it." Orders are capped at two rolls or bags per household until this afternoon, and the first batch sold out within hours Wednesday. They're billed as "special circulating dollar coins," so some could eventually turn up in your change.

Over the past few days, I have seen any number of "good" Democrats say a lot of things (some of them unprintable) that boil down to "You voted for him. We told you so, who cares if you lose that farm." In some of the comments, their joy is palpable.
First, Democrats can't complain about divisiveness, then, when they have a chance to be better, join in the nastiness of modern American politics. Second, Democrats have to accept we have not articulated a coherent rural policy in decades. What reason did we give farmers to vote for us? The fact that we surrendered hundreds of seats in rural areas without contest says a lot.
Many Democrats running in Alabama this year are trying to offer a different approach to rural voters. We want them to know we've heard them and that we will fight to rebuild failing infrastructure, like water and sewer systems. We're going to fight for new infrastructure, like getting high-speed internet to every home in the state. We'll work to shrink the healthcare deserts in rural areas. We'll fight to improve the quality of rural schools, but we will never get elected if all Trump voters hear is, "We told you so..."

| | | Fellow American, I want to tell you about a conversation I'll never forget. **I sat down with Justice Clarence Thomas for his first-ever podcast interview, on my show Verdict.** Before we even started recording, he thanked me. He talked about the thirty years he's known me, and said I'm one of the people who stands up when others wither -- including when he and his wife came under the worst kind of political attack.

Coming from a sitting Justice of the United States Supreme Court, I won't pretend that didn't mean something to me. But the real story that day was his. Justice Thomas grew up dirt poor in Pin Point, Georgia. His family's house burned down when he was six. He lived in a one-room tenement with no indoor plumbing before his grandparents took him in at seven -- a man he calls the greatest he's ever known. His grandfather worked him hard, no excuses and no gloves in the cold. And it was that same grandfather who, when a young and angry Thomas said the country needed to be torn down, asked him a question he says he still can't fully answer: if you destroy it, where do you go instead? That question -- _and his faith_ -- turned his life around. Today he sits on the highest court in the land, and he refuses to let anyone tell him what he's supposed to believe because of the color of his skin. **[That's the America I believe in. It's also the America the radical left is working every single day to tear down.](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=a3447712c8ea4d69b21f5fae24ffd4fd&_e=IFrWlwt2_-mVf-BGUN9rUwaULoBaHzDXBV0pH9y3NL238GyVBzYgZa6VuQwZyV7jJkmK3O4sffem9AbnuxFYcVWRyUSkTt-Or8a7SOSklefrr0tsRDsfiL8USRmQsqPkAOgCUrLmymPGmix3zbxpSg2IjhX0f2kVuhpSFQZ_G0rvJtIOrBKf9-s9RsFwj_GqnwTXnfroQYxYgarurli88vyCf4NRA2DePrA7CPLcnJjdKb65MHLMFjMUlK1Fu9RsBBY81H2VPXBsuTfVm8-53oOH911ZIM-rZ5IaJ8cR7Dfw7oQlh2BHdXtm1nPPPvhk5VSIAi4vQuy0OFh9BfkGIcDrC_Wufzm_094CR9eRrXrYHINoVZguDjn0l-P4qJupfPEG052KiAC59UJCvvRKIbr6kmZdW6kTj3hdRYlYOH0_JJcdqgeQ05Vh1_4eeeaAWAD85MTjBybTA4CrASoWi_9f4sOgxFOT2J6fUTmqp0YzXXo8fEOTn0wsxaqIz0PplA6HP3eLiU94Pr2PFfDNFQSgJWLeCu-m5CobxbE3_dwQrvMdxAYpCD4MNf_aYwur)** **[I need you standing with me. clean_body: His first-ever podcast interview. My show. A story I have to share with you. His first-ever podcast interview. My show. A story I have to share with you. | | | | | | | Fellow American, I want to tell you about a conversation I'll never forget. I sat down with Justice Clarence Thomas for his first-ever podcast interview, on my show Verdict. Before we even started recording, he thanked me. He talked about the thirty years he's known me, and said I'm one of the people who stands up when others wither -- including when he and his wife came under the worst kind of political attack. Coming from a sitting Justice of the United States Supreme Court, I won't pretend that didn't mean something to me. But the real story that day was his. Justice Thomas grew up dirt poor in Pin Point, Georgia. His family's house burned down when he was six. He lived in a one-room tenement with no indoor plumbing before his grandparents took him in at seven -- a man he calls the greatest he's ever known. His grandfather worked him hard, no excuses and no gloves in the cold. And it was that same grandfather who, when a young and angry Thomas said the country needed to be torn down, asked him a question he says he still can't fully answer: if you destroy it, where do you go instead? That question -- and his faith -- turned his life around. Today he sits on the highest court in the land, and he refuses to let anyone tell him what he's supposed to believe because of the color of his skin. I appreciate you more than you know -- Ted CruzU.S. Senator - Texas | | | Paid for by Ted Cruz for Senate | | PO Box 25400 Houston, TX 77265 | | | | ]()

name: Roy Cooper
subject: What happened back in 2016 – illustrated
body:
10,000 votes 10 years ago
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1162&source=&t=1&akid=3179%2E124072%2E8yjpRH) | | | |
---
Peter,
At the end of this message, I’m going to ask you to chip in $5 to my Senate campaign here in North Carolina. [**_If you’re ready to give now, you can use this link to donate._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1162&amount=5&t=8&akid=3179%2E124072%2E8yjpRH)
**Otherwise, please let me explain why your support is so important and what could happen here in North Carolina without it.**
In 2016, I ran to unseat the incumbent Governor – something no one had done in North Carolina for 150 years – but I knew our team could make history and defeat Pat McCrory. In the lead-up, poll after poll had me with a slight lead, and sometimes, more than that. By all accounts, _the momentum was on our side._
[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1162&amount=5&t=9&akid=3179%2E124072%2E8yjpRH)
**However, it was too close to call on election night.** I went to bed leading by fewer than 5,000 votes ... _out of 4.6 million._ Instead of conceding, the incumbent Governor called for a recount, and he spent the next month claiming voter fraud and undermining faith in the democratic process.
[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1162&amount=5&t=10&akid=3179%2E124072%2E8yjpRH)
**Still, democracy won out on Dec. 5, 2016 – and so did we, by 10,277 votes.**
[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1162&amount=5&t=11&akid=3179%2E124072%2E8yjpRH)
Fast-forward 10 years, and, Peter, this current Senate race is starting to remind me a lot of 2016. Just like back then, the momentum appears to be on our side. According to The New York Times, this is the best chance in the entire country for Democrats to flip a Republican-held seat.
**We could’ve just as easily lost in 2016 though. The margin of victory was only 0.22%.**
[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1162&amount=5&t=12&akid=3179%2E124072%2E8yjpRH)_RealClearPolitics, 2016 North Carolina Governor - McCrory vs. Cooper_
That’s why we simply cannot take our foot off the gas this time around. We cannot look at the polls and the predictions and think for a second that we have this in the bag. We cannot give our Republican opponent – or the right-wing super PACs supporting him – an inch.
**I won in 2016 – in the same election that President Trump first won the presidency in North Carolina – only because of grassroots support from people like you. That’s how I plan to win this time, but I need you with me once again.**
[**_Please, Peter: Will you chip in $5, or whatever you can, today to help us flip North Carolina blue and take back the Senate for Democrats?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1162&amount=5&t=13&akid=3179%2E124072%2E8yjpRH)

Roy Cooper

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

**Good Morning!** On this day in 1834, the first Presbyterian missionary in Texas [helped two Methodist preachers](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFyqzAQgOHTiA5mWckYChWvofNrUzLCWsFOZMkjLca5fSa5Qi7w_zPfx225OY6ctv_uQVbeIS-JzhpJhMpCPh-u-BBz9py2kmsNXGg9FgQcWpha0Iu7C79oMa7xdgU_9Q3Z_jqORms9Xprd4jp5QryPCMH44M04Iq6mH-BqPNClYfuTgwl034MG7AbXO-zDij4AhQGUAfIsuXSyk9Db1RC_8otKd8-PJtpd5FmV_qdwVjif59lJ3V1OkRN1uWwK590lv-b8qXCmJIWpKpzDESOnkz2V9klCpd2PJFSaYv3z5Bi5DldlYHs4jr8v-avRy-J3AAAA__-7sn6P) hold a camp meeting on Caney Creek, near present-day Kenney. Peter Hunter Fullinwider had ridden back from his Mississippi wedding that spring. Do you remember what evenings felt like when you were a kid? The whole family at the table by six, a phone call after dinner, maybe the sound of neighbors talking out on the porch. These are five after-dinner habits that once defined American life, and they've all but vanished or been replaced. Join Ayla on _The Flyover Podcast_ as she counts down all five and takes you on a trip down memory lane. [Tune in here](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykzzFuwyAUgOHTwBbrAQ6YgaFLtnTtiLDfI0HCxgLiJLevWvUG3X990v919deQctpun2El11-x-I2eLVPvVD1heYSKMZeCabvV0lpMleaHlyD1CewJlA9LTwf5MXB0M6AVnJww0zQqpaYzvzuj0VgBFqw-I50NKLsIE2YrpqilnXhyPxxYUEKAAjnoIIIUcZYYgaIGNgJh6qUO_U6dXqHF_C4H1WEpK8_u3vvemPpg8sLkpdJcw4ZDfjN5-Qv3gpUW2jqvDvdnyjk1bdgItzWk_Mv0_-4fTn4HAAD__8UwcEA)! body:
I don't trust the polls without verifying.

Friend,

In my years of campaign work, __this__ is my most valuable piece of advice:
_Don 't ever rely on the polls without **[VERIFYING.](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckcGunCAUhp8Gd06Ao6gLF03NJF3cria3S3KEc2fIFbSA2r59w0z7At2RPx-c_-P8eNNv6BYX7t_R02gOp2PS-eHSue6LnQm9s5miN5gxZS25VDUfag4aTXYH6QYrOxqrQFY0iq7vG2iE7KrH2Lbz0IrO4IecOSpsJRrohrlDGua5w8qN5Tk-cBBCtFJdgM_9LOZekLAIBljD981ipnQxa0gUDywzXQhrOa3hYlZfLeMj5y0x-MLklclrIrNHupwuRLKFYPIaYjJMXpXYKBoKuT6On_UnmprqDcs1uO7Za0_W7Z7BRB7dwqQqYVr3aIjBtEqvC_1Ms2EwfX3_Vv9z-Jsb9Bu6e2AwxbOMUEJ_mjWc-Fu_WrywNWQKmcH0sQcb0SUX7kwq9HlbkytyDKbmlTQMJsE5kyoWt1hQmHLciUlFv3R2lsH0LNKD0Ldb_X67CNE1_aCzGFQr-65uu7aKo91OtywuqY41_F4sn3-Y_3P1xyj_BAAA__9RSb17)**_
As the President's 2016 campaign manager, trust me, I witnessed the mainstream media's polling bias first-hand.

So, naturally, when I saw a new survey that claimed to show **[ONLY 61%](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckcGunCAUhp8Gd06Ao6gLF03NJF3cria3S3KEc2fIFbSA2r59w0z7At2RPx-c_-P8eNNv6BYX7t_R02gOp2PS-eHSue6LnQm9s5miN5gxZS25VDUfag4aTXYH6QYrOxqrQFY0iq7vG2iE7KrH2Lbz0IrO4IecOSpsJRrohrlDGua5w8qN5Tk-cBBCtFJdgM_9LOZekLAIBljD981ipnQxa0gUDywzXQhrOa3hYlZfLeMj5y0x-MLklclrIrNHupwuRLKFYPIaYjJMXpXYKBoKuT6On_UnmprqDcs1uO7Za0_W7Z7BRB7dwqQqYVr3aIjBtEqvC_1Ms2EwfX3_Vv9z-Jsb9Bu6e2AwxbOMUEJ_mjWc-Fu_WrywNWQKmcH0sQcb0SUX7kwq9HlbkytyDKbmlTQMJsE5kyoWt1hQmHLciUlFv3R2lsH0LNKD0Ldb_X67CNE1_aCzGFQr-65uu7aKo91OtywuqY41_F4sn3-Y_3P1xyj_BAAA__9RSb17)** of Republican voters are interested in turning out for the midterm elections this November, I knew this was either a catastrophic reality - _**[or one of the phoniest polls I'd ever seen!](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckcGunCAUhp8Gd06Ao6gLF03NJF3cria3S3KEc2fIFbSA2r59w0z7At2RPx-c_-P8eNNv6BYX7t_R02gOp2PS-eHSue6LnQm9s5miN5gxZS25VDUfag4aTXYH6QYrOxqrQFY0iq7vG2iE7KrH2Lbz0IrO4IecOSpsJRrohrlDGua5w8qN5Tk-cBBCtFJdgM_9LOZekLAIBljD981ipnQxa0gUDywzXQhrOa3hYlZfLeMj5y0x-MLklclrIrNHupwuRLKFYPIaYjJMXpXYKBoKuT6On_UnmprqDcs1uO7Za0_W7Z7BRB7dwqQqYVr3aIjBtEqvC_1Ms2EwfX3_Vv9z-Jsb9Bu6e2AwxbOMUEJ_mjWc-Fu_WrywNWQKmcH0sQcb0SUX7kwq9HlbkytyDKbmlTQMJsE5kyoWt1hQmHLciUlFv3R2lsH0LNKD0Ldb_X67CNE1_aCzGFQr-65uu7aKo91OtywuqY41_F4sn3-Y_3P1xyj_BAAA__9RSb17)**_

**[That's why I immediately partnered up with my friends in Senate GOP leadership to get to the TRUTH by conducting a review of our 2026 Voter Verification Initiative.](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckcGunCAUhp8Gd06Ao6gLF03NJF3cria3S3KEc2fIFbSA2r59w0z7At2RPx-c_-P8eNNv6BYX7t_R02gOp2PS-eHSue6LnQm9s5miN5gxZS25VDUfag4aTXYH6QYrOxqrQFY0iq7vG2iE7KrH2Lbz0IrO4IecOSpsJRrohrlDGua5w8qN5Tk-cBBCtFJdgM_9LOZekLAIBljD981ipnQxa0gUDywzXQhrOa3hYlZfLeMj5y0x-MLklclrIrNHupwuRLKFYPIaYjJMXpXYKBoKuT6On_UnmprqDcs1uO7Za0_W7Z7BRB7dwqQqYVr3aIjBtEqvC_1Ms2EwfX3_Vv9z-Jsb9Bu6e2AwxbOMUEJ_mjWc-Fu_WrywNWQKmcH0sQcb0SUX7kwq9HlbkytyDKbmlTQMJsE5kyoWt1hQmHLciUlFv3R2lsH0LNKD0Ldb_X67CNE1_aCzGFQr-65uu7aKo91OtywuqY41_F4sn3-Y_3P1xyj_BAAA__9RSb17)**

Friend, the only source I trust 100% is grassroots voters like _YOU_ - and your direct, unfiltered opinions.

Hey friends,
Thanks for coming back for Part 2 of my conversation with Brandon Puttbrese!
[**Click here to LISTEN NOW!**](https://us.list-manage.com/122WUvZhHMe?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)****

#### [**Listen or watch**](https://us.list-manage.com/VuzTWuEUw_i?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)**now wherever you get your podcasts. 🎧**

Brandon is back for round two, and we've got a lot to cover. We get into Tennessee's abortion ban and a personal bill I brought to add narrow exceptions, a wave of bills passed after Charlie Kirk's death that Brandon and I think function more like censorship than free speech, and some of the most brazen corporate giveaways I've seen in a while, including an entire regulatory framework built for one billionaire's Nashville tunnel project.
We also talk about a real bipartisan win: a voting rights restoration bill that took years to pass, and close on what's _actually_ giving Brandon hope right now.
This one covers a lot of ground, and I hope it sheds some light on what's actually being prioritized in our state legislature.
Check out the show notes for this episode and others [here](https://us.list-manage.com/nh39VDlceJw?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)!
Thank you for being here,
**Gloria**

Every word in this letter comes directly from me, and I hope you’ll spare just a minute to hear me out.

Let me start off by saying the rising tide of socialism in this country should have real Americans terrified.

**First, it was Zohran Mamdani in New York. Then, it was Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan. Now, another Far Left socialist just won a Democrat Senate primary in Florida in a stunning upset!**

body:
America has always been the place of big ideas.
# [](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/46?t=1&akid=81%2E42639%2EJYCKRI)
Today in America, we have more wealth and income inequality than at any time since the 1920s. We spend more money per person on health care, yet get worse results than just about every advanced country in the world. Families cannot afford to spend time with their newborn children or take care of a loved one when they are sick and need help. And we have a corrupt system of campaign finance where the wealthiest are able to buy elections to keep the status quo in place.
Now is not the time for small thinking. Now is not the time for the same old wonky milquetoast incrementalism.
When Democrats take back power in November we must think BIG.
It may sometimes feel like that’s impossible, but for a long time America was a place of big ideas.
🇺🇸 Our foundation as a free and democratic nation.
🛤️ Construction of the transcontinental railroad
🛣️ The interstate highway system, and the roads and bridges that connected the country.
⚡️ We electrified every community.
👵🏼 We created Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid.
🚀 We put a man on the moon.
So we do not have to accept small things. We can dream bigger.
I recently introduced what I think is a big idea in Congress. It's called the Build America Plan. It's built around three pillars.
Now, if you prefer your emails from politicians to be the ones with over-the-top fundraising requests, then the rest of this message may not be for you. Because I am about to lay out the three pillars of this plan.
**First, build it here.** America should not be so reliant on foreign (many hostile) suppliers for the products we need every day. We should strengthen our supply chains, modernize our electric grid, and create good-paying jobs that can't be shipped overseas. It's not a level playing field for the American worker. That's why our bill creates a sovereign wealth fund that makes real investments to fight fire with fire against foreign competitors.
**Second, build it strong.** A four-year degree is a great path for some people — it shouldn't be the only path. We should be investing in apprenticeships, career and technical education, and the skilled trades that keep this country running. That starts with increasing students' exposure to trades education in high school. That means more classes, more mentors, and more funding for pathways other than college, so that our young folks have real options for their futures.
**Third, build it right.** If we're going to build the future, let's build it cleaner than anyone else. American workers shouldn't have to compete unfairly against countries that pollute more, pay workers less, and undercut businesses that play by the rules.
I want the next generation to know and inherit the America that builds. The America that rolls up its sleeves and attacks its challenges head-on. Where we're proud to stamp "Made in America" after creating something amazing.
That's the Build America Plan.
I hope you'll support it, follow me and its progress, and that together we can do something great for the future of the country we all love.
Thanks for reading,
Chris Deluzio

The grassroots is the only thing stopping it. 2 months left. | Peter, Two months from today, the most important midterm election in a generation gets decided. And right now, heading into the final stretch, the socialist movement is having the best political cycle in American history. This is not an exaggeration. This is not campaign rhetoric. New York City elected a self-described democratic socialist as its mayor. He was sworn in alongside Bernie Sanders. His movement supports abolishing the Senate, abolishing ICE, abolishing prisons, and seizing private property from American citizens. In Michigan , a socialist-aligned candidate won a Democratic Senate primary. Right here in Florida , a card-carrying member of the Democratic Socialists of America, backed by Ilhan Omar and Rashida Tlaib, won a Senate primary by double digits — spending less than $1 million to defeat a $16.3 million establishment candidate. If this is not a wake-up call for every conservative in America, I don't know what is. The alarm bells are ringing. The signs are everywhere. Primary after primary. State after state. The socialist movement is not lurking on the fringes of the Democrat Party anymore. It is the Democrat Party's future. And it is two months away from proving it can win general elections. Here is what makes this moment different from every other cycle conservatives have faced. The socialist movement does not need billionaire donors to win. It does not need the establishment. Nixon beat a candidate who had outraised her 16 to 1. Mamdani took New York City with grassroots organizing and small-dollar donations. These candidates are winning on enthusiasm, organizing, and the energy of a movement that genuinely believes 2026 is their moment. The only thing that beats a movement is another movement. And right now, the conservative grassroots is the only firewall standing between the socialist surge and a wave of victories on November 3. This November, there are 435 U.S. House seats on the ballot nationwide. 34 U.S. Senate seats. Governor's races in 36 states. Hundreds of state legislative seats that will shape redistricting, policy, and the pipeline of future candidates for the next decade. The Republican majority in Congress — the majority that gives President Trump the ability to pass his agenda, fund border security, cut taxes, and advance the America First platform — is on the line in every single one of those House races. The grassroots conservative movement is what wins this. Not the super PACs. Without that grassroots army, we cannot fund the voter contact operations. We cannot support the candidates in competitive districts. We cannot run the turnout programs in the counties where margins are decided by hundreds of votes. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters this week that ICE agents can--and very likely will--be deployed to polling places if he so chooses.
Mullin said ICE will conduct operations at polling places "if there is a threat" or if "we're serving a warrant on someone that we have been actively tracking down. If we're serving a warrant we will be where we need to be."
The Secretary's comments are not reasonable and, importantly, they are not legal: federal law prohibits and imposes a possible penalty of up to 5 years in prison for federal officials who order or knowingly order "armed men" to a location where an election is taking place. The law also allows disqualification from federal office for officials who violate it.
Put very plainly: armed ICE agents cannot make arrests and conduct routine law enforcement operations at polling places while an election is taking place. Full stop.

# What's new in Grok Imagine Image 2.0
[grok-imagine-image-2.0](https://x.ai/news/grok-imagine-image-2?utm_source=sendgrid&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=imagine-image-2-updates-email) now defaults to quality: auto. On November 2, grok-imagine-image-quality is retired and will serve 2.0 at quality: low, $0.01 less per image.

What's New

Auto quality quality now accepts auto, the default. Auto picks the tier per request to cut latency without lowering output quality. Today it serves low for generation and medium for editing; you are billed at the tier served. [Quality docs](https://docs.x.ai/developers/model-capabilities/images/generation?utm_source=sendgrid&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=imagine-image-2-updates-email#quality).
---
Up to 5 reference images Editing takes up to 5 reference images per request, up from 3. For example: one character, three props and one location, then prompt the scene you want them in. [Multi-image editing docs](https://docs.x.ai/developers/model-capabilities/images/multi-image-editing?utm_source=sendgrid&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=imagine-image-2-updates-email).
New aspect ratios Generation and editing now support 21:9 and 5:2 for widescreen and banner formats. [Aspect ratio docs](https://docs.x.ai/developers/model-capabilities/images/generation?utm_source=sendgrid&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=imagine-image-2-updates-email#aspect-ratio).

---

Improved text rendering

On November 2, grok-imagine-image-quality is retired and will serve grok-imagine-image-2.0 at quality: low. No code change needed. Output will differ, so consider testing 2.0 at low before then.

2.0 at quality: low is $0.01 less per image than grok-imagine-image-quality. clean_body: Two months from today, America votes and the House Majority gets decided. Here is exactly what that means for every conservative in this country. | Fellow Conservative, Two months from today, America votes. I want to take a moment before the final sprint begins to tell you exactly what is on the line. Not the talking points. Not the fundraising pitch. Just the truth about what November 3rd actually decides. Republicans hold it by two seats. Two. The DCCC has spent all year mapping every vulnerable district across the country and building a financial machine to flip enough seats to hand Hakeem Jeffries the gavel. If they succeed, here is what happens on Day 1: investigations into President Trump begin. Tax cuts get threatened. The SAVE Act gets buried. And the Congress that was elected to deliver results for the American people gets turned into a weapon pointed at the man those people chose to lead them. | Every executive order. Every border policy. Every energy win. Every piece of legislation that has delivered results for working Americans over the last two years. A Democrat majority doesn't just slow it down. It uses the full power of Congress to reverse it, investigate it, and dismantle it piece by piece. They don't just want to stop the America First agenda. The DSA now has over 100,000 members. They beat three sitting House Democrats in primaries this cycle. There are 11 openly socialist candidates on the November ballot running on Medicare for All, abolishing ICE, and the Green New Deal. This is not fringe. It is not theoretical. It is on the ballot. And if the House flips, every one of those candidates caucuses with Jeffries and pushes that agenda forward from inside the majority. Free markets. Individual liberty. A government that works for the people and not the other way around. A country where hard work still means something and Washington stays out of the way of the people doing it. These are not partisan talking points. They are the foundation this country was built on. You hear it every time you turn on the news... _" Donald Trump wants to be King." "Donald Trump is a dictator." "Donald Trump is a Nazi."_

Increasingly, they proudly call for outright socialism!

**This is an alarming wake-up call. A warning to Americans across the country to fight for our constitutional rights and our free-market system. **

Because if the radical left gets their way, these things will be gone forever...

I'll never stop defending America, our Constitution, our free market economy, and our Judeo-Christian traditions. And I'll never stop calling out the leftists who want to tear our country down.

I know you won't either!

I'm doing everything I can to rally our fellow freedom-lovers to the fight, through my books, my radio show, and my TV show.

_**But one of the most important things I do is work with my colleagues at Landmark Legal Foundation.**_

Landmark is here to protect liberty, property rights, constitutionalism...in other words, what you read in the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution.

Landmark Legal Foundation battles the Left in court. Their top-notch team of lawyers files "friend of the court" briefs to back up major cases against government abuses. These briefs present the strongest possible argument for the constitutional position and **help convince judges to do the right thing.**

My friends at Landmark fight hard to save our country. And now, I hope you'll join their fight.

Greg Abbott has been the Governor of Texas for 12 years.
**_That means he is the only governor our state’s 7th graders have ever known for their entire lives,_** and the governor that most young adults in Texas have had for most of theirs.
