Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. By Sept. 30, Colorado’s Department of Personnel and Administration
is due to produce its annual tally of contracts covered by the state
Procurement Code — the number awarded, the initial dollar amounts
recorded, and the share that went to service-disabled veteran-owned
small businesses.

The last three tallies were wrong by hundreds of millions to billions
of dollars, the state auditor has found. And this year, the department
has said it does not plan to send the report to lawmakers at all.

The Office of the State Auditor laid it out in Report 2556P, a
performance audit of the state’s contracting goal for
service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses, released in May.

_Colorado hiked the cost of registering a vehicle, then built a
penalty machine to squeeze drivers who can't keep up._

*
REVENUE KEEPS CLIMBING: Colorado collected a record $45.1 million in
late vehicle-registration fees in FY 2024-25, a roughly 36% jump in
three years, driven partly by a 2022 law that expanded what the state
can collect.

*
CRACKDOWNS ARE MULTIPLYING: Denver, Colorado Springs, El Paso County
and Colorado State Patrol have all run repeated "zero-tolerance"
enforcement surges, issuing hundreds of citations at a time and
threatening impoundment for plates expired over a year.

*
WORKING FAMILIES BEAR THE COST: With 877,084 Colorado households
already unable to cover basic living costs per United For ALICE, the
piece argues lawmakers should audit and cut the stack of fees, taxes
and surcharges before piling on more enforcement.

| | Peter,
---
If you ever doubted we could win America's youth back from the Left...

If you ever wondered whether we'd lost the next generation for good...

If you ever sat up at night -- watching the news, seeing what's happening in our schools, our culture, our country -- and thought, _" Is it already too late?" _

You're not alone.

A lot of good people have been asking the same question.

**But I want to tell you something that might just change how you feel about the future of this country... **

Just one year ago, Turning Point USA's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.

That was no small feat.

Starting a single chapter today takes serious courage. Students get mocked. Threatened. Investigated. Sometimes even physically attacked.

So reaching 1,200 chapters already felt like a miracle.

_Then Charlie called me... _

He said: "Andrew, I love what we're doing with our high school program -- but we've got to move faster."

I told him, "We are."

Charlie replied, "No you're not thinking what I'm thinking... I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I laughed. I told him, "Charlie, there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said, "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

Without skipping a beat, Charlie said, "Okay, great. Let's do 27,000!"
I'll be honest -- I froze.

We didn't have the numbers. We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the roadmap yet.

But he wasn't fazed.

He said, "Don't worry. We'll figure it out. We'll do it together."

That was Charlie.

He didn't think small. He didn't move slow. He didn't settle for "maybe someday."

He believed in going now.

And he believed that if the mission was right, the path would reveal itself.

He chased what others only dreamed about... and turned what others thought impossible into reality.

That's why he built Turning Point USA in the first place.

That's why tens of thousands of students were inspired by Charlie to start chapters of their own -- _many in schools where they were explicitly told not to. _

**And that 's why today -- less than a year later -- we're not in 1,200 schools anymore: **

We're in 3,300.

That's roughly 13% of all high schools in America.

Eight states have officially partnered with Club America to bring our chapters into every school statewide.

✅ Florida
✅ Texas
✅ Tennessee
✅ Oklahoma
✅ Montana
✅ Nebraska
✅ Arkansas
✅ Indiana

And we're just getting started.

Think about that: 13% of America's youth now have a place at school where they can say it's okay to love this country...

That it's okay to be bold. That it's okay to believe in God, in family, and in freedom.

_That 's what Club America is about... _

**Giving the next generation a place where they can find their courage, develop grit, and learn how to lead the fight for their country. **

_But now, Peter, the question is... _

**What will it take to bring Club America to the next 3,300 schools? What will it take to bring it to all 27,000? **

Because here's the truth:

These students aren't just signing up. _They 're stepping up. _

They're leading chapters in schools where America is attacked... where they're often targeted for daring to say what they believe... and where speaking the truth is dangerous.

But that isn't stopping them.

They're still showing up. They're speaking out. And they're growing stronger than ever.

They're becoming exactly the kind of young patriots Charlie believed in -- not just bold, _but brave_. Not just loud, but _principled_.

**Every time a student starts a new chapter, we make sure they 're not standing alone. **

**We send them an activism kit -- American flags, pocket Constitutions, chapter materials, and leadership tools. **

These kits give student leaders everything they need to rally their peers and stand strong on their campuses.

Each one costs just $25 to pack and ship.

**[If you’re able to, I hope you’ll help send a kit to the next student who raises their hand to lead by making your gift to Turning Point USA today.](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=3c5d6c83aa194c9fb80624d315d9b0b7&_e=PZaHsiIGG66Lb0gdouMrgKEslzUsqLuzFHpaZ44ZzOTCwtN1gc9m-rI42Fb1p8pk-uEpp3K8s-nMyyrLe9JZFixzEea9Y_d-xM6hEFf6v671bXC76-p8h-N6MWWbi3g9XV6LgOC4kP8y_iEodFTCDMJcU_KB2hk_Z9hlt8C_H_faLCldInH-Z3AtbdTbdUWzkGbl3qhSvGUBn5mr8R-KXUSjN1nMlKTyTcXj5QTmzh705efQuwvNFReJbOS702x9VbN04dVZAE1FZSJPIekhricSyt5IquhcxgEESUg8nP3URkHjsiJYyDJogQhEDNo1HCTjOtOGGy4sBXNObEkYrr3UzuPJYjqsXOjgdUqVZUyjvEpxiSULW1O7UJxWnz9CmwketYly1a80vu9c2pCTCZcy1nkmK7KtflMP35qVZCNCiX91FsAzW6UmR91wUvs63-qo19GCcIPRHVMVENMRTI6Gf_gY0BCl_hYvXb_bCouXb5Oa0BQIAEFhQMVdjdxbWXjbMmGEgr0imtrs6h2XKmnyEieWAH8fA8BbFtjyQR53J63K5qS9pVMgUP_0q7XRMRoMG3lDz8AOaBl9StwlE7rAcGM7dvhZMp6G9g6M4gWA-T4IhBleDM3AB32ghrLQBPj0gwVvJwnY5eGHJd0gxNsrxVx5RjQUMFUKOw2JkAgOCs3xOgoPt747hUSLdsjmhpXWpQFRkAYzodgCI41GjfynPJ7iOVWp_xemJKfoZTM%3D)**

It's up to us to finish what he started.

One chapter. One student. One school at a time.

Let's move faster. Let's push further. Let's get this done -- for Charlie, and for the country we all love.

That includes **reproductive **freedom. Because the power to decide if, when, and how to grow your family is deeply connected to your economic security. When politicians take that decision away, they can make it harder for people to stay in school, keep a job, care for their families, and plan for their future. That’s why we’re proud to have frontline union members standing alongside us in our fight for reproductive freedom in Virginia. **This week, SEIU Virginia State Council endorsed the constitutional amendment to ensure reproductive freedom for all Virginians, recognizing that _“workers’ rights and the right to make our own reproductive health care decisions are intrinsically linked.”_**

clean_body: You can’t have economic freedom without reproductive freedom. | | | | | | | | | | Hi friend,= Labor Day is a time to recognize that workers are the backbone of Virginia’s economy, and to remember that every worker deserves the freedom to build a secure future for themselves and their families. That includes reproductive freedom. Because the power to decide if, when, and how to grow your family is deeply connected to your economic security. When politicians take that decision away, they can make it harder for people to stay in school, keep a job, care for their families, and plan for their future. That’s why we’re proud to have frontline union members standing alongside us in our fight for reproductive freedom in Virginia. This week, SEIU Virginia State Council endorsed the constitutional amendment to ensure reproductive freedom for all Virginians, recognizing that “workers’ rights and the right to make our own reproductive health care decisions are intrinsically linked.” = = And they’re not alone. Across Virginia, labor leaders and reproductive freedom advocates are coming together to knock doors, talk with their neighbors, and build a movement that recognizes that economic freedom and reproductive freedom go hand in hand. = = Your contribution will help Virginians for Reproductive Freedom educate voters on what a YES on 1 vote means, fight misinformation, and rally the support we’ll need to win a historic VICTORY on November 3. With two weeks until Early Voting begins, we need your help to send the message that reproductive freedom is key to a future where all working families can thrive. In solidarity, Han Jones Campaign Manager P.S. This Labor Day, put your values to work! or = to help fuel our historic movement to protect Virginians’ access to reproductive health care and economic freedom. | | | | | | | | | Virginians for Reproductive Freedom600 Pennsylvania Ave SE Unit 15845 Washington, DC 20003 | | | |

Peter, With just over 60 days to election day, Republican extremists know they are losing. It is why Keith Self is burning these final weeks on a recall stunt and lashing out in increasingly bizarre ways that do nothing to lower the price of groceries.
---
[ **FLIP TX-03 AND PUT SERVICE OVER SELF** ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt83D0wYpnqLib7Kr5si2_BwngKIRu2EFYFw_A9mSghidFOKVxdo0OVGWORhDr-2WeKXnUdrM_C0ArxpM1J8D99cqrWTaLSx97jcgy-0-c1-CPi_T4yUdO-4ItzQX5Zn8cLJlXWVgm0gDOn_hYJEBhJt3YW3gyhpwWXjtz0loc0T6LJbcOh7a5EANKdEhJb3kiXuv1Q_LHuvU9LbTpN7sGwbnFvErmGD6IX0Gfs0H4p7DeHbhUhlt4GFUElS16yZP3-pn3xag0c4pL7-SPB8L00z_6gXeulnB_I80SgkbyXu8qyRjinp04mMYvKAFe7dPcUnI3UlgGsOhqq5APOeX4RP0TErbmK67PuBOybmV0M25zhZwV8-nyDnE2TwSLBhkhAw/4tq/XtRP7uCISH-N3X3AoQ1eCg/h1/h001.OipFzdZ_uMYRCGCNCtxlKFOGWvrDAZgZL2Grs9bfof0)
---
Keith Self loves to paint Democrats as out-of-touch wildcards who have no idea what "Main Street America" cares about. Well, let's run the tape on what these so-called serious statesmen have been up to lately: Trump just renamed Lake Ontario to _"Lake America"_ because Canada hurt his feelings in a trade fight. Pete Hegseth is in his office filming testosterone videos while our carrier crews break down and nearly starve at sea. And our own congressman spent his summer declaring airport foot-washing stations a "Sharia takeover". Melting down over a lake, a sink, and a zoning permit - _and they call US snowflakes._ [**Chip in and help us replace the circus with somebody serious.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt83D0wYpnqLib7Kr5si2_BwngKIRu2EFYFw_A9mSghidF2MqCnW4JEVk87yrScivHU36cFyMc36ET_19uj1m5D7xLgVzBhRo5XtYADPSsmlUrG96E--T14zKGvAG3TVrZghXeVRsuYzDSsjVP7Z7IxbdTXc1NBDG7ovJGSCklob1xigKiY6Vc3rlBSwbpR8oiVPDVk7G_6uJwq1VMrRgPe61d8F5qDa_kobQgrjGxeLP6GFyHPKWRtfDKmWcLNgGjGtQRQuLP6Riud3MnEN7dQxQXzw5Cq2-i4w8xazqn8Un16I41jUtQALkvnc4xSnzlEQYzniJyJzqGp4NQlXmsPSSzhv_iE-Vq3J6nTMEV94ssEyGuDy7dvK3Nu1epHl-yTg/4tq/XtRP7uCISH-N3X3AoQ1eCg/h2/h001.VOAFKgXCmnVVBtBGr-0AF1c1r7Lgk5x0pIuOuaD1HF8) Out on the doors, I hear the same thing from Republicans, Democrats, and independents alike. Nobody feels heard over the noise. And I talked about this at the recent Democracy Summit:
---
| [ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt83D0wYpnqLib7Kr5si2_BwngKIRu2EFYFw_A9mSghidF97FYKqh-ZdmSdvbQ3HXHSvDywX3iKjSjTxp6YMb_walO1YlMkAyLige8iwHN0TBb_Szfy2H0uVC-8nfBEF1ho_Ekb7-_fxTsG4X5Om75bHpFJIHMO1Mq1y3g9ltMqQ_LOBQ0RVc6LDjZqcGMaW8eaV7I3Klsb1-3D88ex4RvAcMvRQHLe-i6zuwGHuj_X8IuxrnDaaNTFWYwjk7k0npt430BGZcV-NgvYGAoRTx8M1NZn2TgUK2x2Ayr_KjULRtxldTiI4Xk3JQyYdMKTJ-Wr_9UNdRFC8lJDp0JU74UxHdABJFJ3FowjrXp_0ieH7BTMndznpHNGl2rwXT2F83rzw/4tq/XtRP7uCISH-N3X3AoQ1eCg/h3/h001.2-Y9Cf5qmEPqAaXPNHYnKwCJeIg7EFjo-lSZbpu1nSo)
---
That is how you get an illegal war in Iran and a government bought by special interests while Congress runs for the cameras instead of the country. **Our campaign has taken the opposite approach from day one.** We lead with community and service first, whether that is pitching in when storms tear through this district or pulling up a chair for folks who gave up on politics years ago. That is the work of public service, even if this administration has abandoned it for a traveling carnival of grievance and stunts. **Republicans and folks who wrote off politics years ago have been opening their doors to us, and the secret is there is no secret.** We showed up and stayed to listen. We do not see eye to eye on everything, but we land in the same place on the big one: _that all this chaos is not working for regular people._ Neighbors of every political stripe sitting at the same table and working out where we go from here together. **To me, that is American freedom defined.** [**In just over 60 days, this district gets to choose between the circus and the work. Chip in today and help us make sure the work wins.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt83D0wYpnqLib7Kr5si2_BwngKIRu2EFYFw_A9mSghidFyu8jf1rj2xitYcqAgbWMyR1KnFVfhvgHJSBKhKDOZy_BKg7Efp6c-QAaL4JY4Pe1vBqI_n6aWrh9JVBQlV53tQl6qHXK4QPp-GnIxK4BXrHhkNP9xEHShjs9R57Hy-xBXMycCabrOM6JldOHTTvYONbdq2513kb-7Ou3ExNAirgT-z5o0E07ZyiIAERzKKN2vPxcc05JMmsX40j3fER6okXN-pcCW4JhgLaYnuKZNewmpHf4GIRJrcCTseEfxutLsp8CJOMkhjaDQQovtJEMs2mG9iG44aMI1Col95KBsPi87lyPcduBWvrk9YBiXCttVXGCPpnvcSTftq8-NLAukw/4tq/XtRP7uCISH-N3X3AoQ1eCg/h4/h001.MhFKRItB13nchS4id_PYzAa14QUqf38h0D-PzZ-d7N0) Very respectfully, Evan Hunt Democratic Nominee TX-03

clean_body: Renaming lakes and recall stunts don’t make life more affordable | | Peter, With just over 60 days to election day, Republican extremists know they are losing. It is why Keith Self is burning these final weeks on a recall stunt and lashing out in increasingly bizarre ways that do nothing to lower the price of groceries. Keith Self loves to paint Democrats as out-of-touch wildcards who have no idea what "Main Street America" cares about. Well, let's run the tape on what these so-called serious statesmen have been up to lately: Trump just renamed Lake Ontario to "Lake America" because Canada hurt his feelings in a trade fight. Pete Hegseth is in his office filming testosterone videos while our carrier crews break down and nearly starve at sea. And our own congressman spent his summer declaring airport foot-washing stations a "Sharia takeover". Melting down over a lake, a sink, and a zoning permit - and they call US snowflakes. Out on the doors, I hear the same thing from Republicans, Democrats, and independents alike. Nobody feels heard over the noise. And I talked about this at the recent Democracy Summit: | That is how you get an illegal war in Iran and a government bought by special interests while Congress runs for the cameras instead of the country. Our campaign has taken the opposite approach from day one. We lead with community and service first, whether that is pitching in when storms tear through this district or pulling up a chair for folks who gave up on politics years ago. That is the work of public service, even if this administration has abandoned it for a traveling carnival of grievance and stunts. Republicans and folks who wrote off politics years ago have been opening their doors to us, and the secret is there is no secret. We showed up and stayed to listen. We do not see eye to eye on everything, but we land in the same place on the big one: that all this chaos is not working for regular people. Neighbors of every political stripe sitting at the same table and working out where we go from here together. To me, that is American freedom defined. | | | I just sat down with Wolf Blitzer on CNN — I was brought on because I sit on the House Intelligence Committee — to talk about where this war with Iran actually stands. I didn't hold back. I told him plainly: **Trump and his MAGA sycophants have turned this into a game of whack-a-mole.** This administration keeps escalating without a strategy, without an endgame, and without listening to the people whose job it is to know better. Even top generals have advised against expanding operations further!

body:
From Coast to Coast

| | | [ ](www.forwardparty.com)
---
### Peter —
We’d like to highlight more candidate endorsements this week. Adding to our slate of federal candidates are two Navy veterans who meet the standard we value at Forward Party. They are John Gregory Vincent of South Carolina, running for U.S. House (SC-07) and Bob Smith of California, running for U.S. House (CA-24). They are on opposite coasts and opposite sides of the political spectrum, but both are running because they believe the communities they want to serve deserve representation that actually serves them. John Gregory Vincent is running as a Democrat and Bob Smith is running as a Republican. As we have argued for years, the letter next to the name should not matter. Forward Party endorses candidates based on simple principles: are they prepared to serve their constituents, work with people who don't share their politics and focus on delivering results rather than performing for their base? In both cases, the answer is yes.
* * *
| Meet John Gregory Vincent Democratic Candidate — U.S. House
South Carolina's 7th Congressional District
---
John Gregory Vincent spent 20 years in the Navy, retired as a Command Master Chief responsible for the welfare and training of service members across seven bases and five military branches, and came home to South Carolina to spend the next chapter of his career in service to his community.
He served on the Board of Directors of the Augusta Kiwanis. He is the Small and Minority Business co-chair for the Florence Chamber of Commerce. He is involved with the committee supporting the Veterans Park in Florence. And he has been sober for more than two decades, which he speaks about publicly and directly, working to reduce the stigma that keeps people from seeking treatment.
His campaign is built around four areas that reflect what he has heard in his district: affordability, jobs and small businesses and farms, schools, healthcare and veterans' services, and government accountability and the federal budget. South Carolina's 7th District deserves a representative who has spent his career studying what it means to serve. Vincent has been doing that work his entire life.
Meet Bob Smith Republican Candidate — U.S. House
California's 24th Congressional District
---
Bob Smith spent more than 26 years in the Navy as a combat veteran and engineer. He was named the U.S. Navy Engineer of the Year in 2023 and received the Humanitarian Service Medal for his work with international disaster relief operations. He is now running in California's Central Coast with the same engineering discipline he brought to advanced weapons systems and international disaster relief.
His community engagement in California's Central Coast has crossed partisan lines in ways that are not commonly seen. He has volunteered with his local Republican Party on data analysis and canvassing. He has also worked on his wife's Democratic city council campaign. He coaches youth sports and mentors young athletes.
His campaign focuses on affordability, education, energy and water, immigration, and national defense. All are framed around their direct impact on the safety and economic security of Central Coast families. Bob's approach to every problem he has ever faced is a testament to his training as an engineer: evaluate the options and put the best solution forward.
* * *
**Why Forward Endorses Democrats and Republicans**
The Forward Party is building a different theory of representation, one that answers to constituents rather than to partisan interests and is willing to work with whoever is serious about getting things done for the American people.
Forward Party's Fulcrum Strategy leans on the argument that across the ideological spectrum, there are people who are more interested in governing than in performing on the stage of partisan theatre. This supports that approach in building a bloc of elected officials willing to act independently of party leadership on consequential votes, ultimately helping to shift the incentive in Congress away from party loyalty and toward earning support on the merits of legislation.
A Democrat from South Carolina and a Republican from California who share that operating principle are more aligned with what Congress is supposed to do than two members from the same party who vote in lockstep with their parties on every issue. That is the Forward Party's primary premise. John Gregory Vincent and Bob Smith are this week's evidence for it.

**Both are the kind of people Congress is supposed to have more of, and currently has far too few of.**
* * *
November 3rd is 61 days away. The Forward Party has candidates on the ballot in South Carolina, California, Ohio, Montana, New York, Idaho, South Dakota, Colorado, Minnesota, Utah, and across the country. Every one of them is evidence of the same thing: good representation does not require a party. It requires the right person.
---
---

And he has been sober for more than two decades, which he speaks about publicly and directly, working to reduce the stigma that keeps people from seeking treatment. His campaign is built around four areas that reflect what he has heard in his district: affordability, jobs and small businesses and farms, schools, healthcare and veterans' services, and government accountability and the federal budget. South Carolina's 7th District deserves a representative who has spent his career studying what it means to serve. Vincent has been doing that work his entire life. Meet Bob Smith Republican Candidate — U.S. House California's 24th Congressional District Bob Smith spent more than 26 years in the Navy as a combat veteran and engineer. He was named the U.S. Navy Engineer of the Year in 2023 and received the Humanitarian Service Medal for his work with international disaster relief operations. He is now running in California's Central Coast with the same engineering discipline he brought to advanced weapons systems and international disaster relief. His community engagement in California's Central Coast has crossed partisan lines in ways that are not commonly seen. He has volunteered with his local Republican Party on data analysis and canvassing. He has also worked on his wife's Democratic city council campaign. He coaches youth sports and mentors young athletes. His campaign focuses on affordability, education, energy and water, immigration, and national defense. All are framed around their direct impact on the safety and economic security of Central Coast families. Bob's approach to every problem he has ever faced is a testament to his training as an engineer: evaluate the options and put the best solution forward. Why Forward Endorses Democrats and Republicans The Forward Party is building a different theory of representation, one that answers to constituents rather than to partisan interests and is willing to work with whoever is serious about getting things done for the American people. Forward Party's Fulcrum Strategy leans on the argument that across the ideological spectrum, there are people who are more interested in governing than in performing on the stage of partisan theatre. This supports that approach in building a bloc of elected officials willing to act independently of party leadership on consequential votes, ultimately helping to shift the incentive in Congress away from party loyalty and toward earning support on the merits of legislation. A Democrat from South Carolina and a Republican from California who share that operating principle are more aligned with what Congress is supposed to do than two members from the same party who vote in lockstep with their parties on every issue. That is the Forward Party's primary premise. John Gregory Vincent and Bob Smith are this week's evidence for it. Both are the kind of people Congress is supposed to have more of, and currently has far too few of. November 3rd is 61 days away. The Forward Party has candidates on the ballot in South Carolina, California, Ohio, Montana, New York, Idaho, South Dakota, Colorado, Minnesota, Utah, and across the country. Every one of them is evidence of the same thing: good representation does not require a party. It requires the right person. In case you missed it, we had Rep. Kevin Kiley on the podcast last week with host Lindsey Drath for a discussion on leading with integrity in Washington. Their conversations explore why experienced political leaders are stepping away from party labels, what voters are asking for, and whether independent candidates can offer a different approach to governing. name: David Hogg
subject: Mitch McConnell: paid leave for senators, not for you
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
Mitch McConnell has been out of the Senate for months — and still gets his full paycheck. Why shouldn't working families get the same?
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260903-1&t=1&akid=3966%2E587540%2E6AimSn)
Peter,
**Mitch McConnell hasn't cast a vote in the Senate since June 11. He's missed 60 roll call votes** — on the defense budget, Iran legislation, and Trump administration nominees. Kentucky's governor has publicly called on him to prove he can still serve, or resign.
Meanwhile, McConnell is still collecting his _full_ Senate paycheck.
**He can be missing from his job for months and get paid. But millions of American workers can't take a single week off to care for a newborn or a sick parent without risking their financial security.**
That's wrong. And it's time we did something about it.
**Here’s my suggestion for Congressional Democrats: introduce national paid sick and parental leave — and call it the MITCH Act.**
**The Maintaining Income Through Caregiving and Health Act would guarantee that working Americans get the same deal Mitch McConnell gets:** the ability to take time away from work when they need it, without losing their paycheck.
If you can be absent from your job for months on end as a U.S. Senator and still collect your full tax-payer funded salary, working parents and caregivers deserve the same.
This isn't complicated. It's about basic fairness. It's about recognizing that workers have families, responsibilities, health issues, and lives outside of their jobs. And it's about holding our elected officials to a standard that reflects the dignity and respect every American deserves.
If McConnell can take a months-long absence and get paid, why can't a new parent take a few weeks off? Why can't someone caring for a sick relative take time off without going broke? Why are working families forced to choose between a paycheck and their health or that of a loved one, while a senator gets both?
Leaders We Deserve is fighting to elect the next generation of leaders who will actually take on fights like this — leaders who won't just talk about fairness, but will introduce bold, creative legislation and hold their colleagues accountable.
We need resources to keep building that movement. To recruit, train, and fund candidates who show up and fight for working families.
**[Will you chip in today to help us elect leaders who will make bills like the MITCH Act a reality? It's time to make the rules work for everyone — not just the politicians in Washington.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260903_1_mitch.vdWBUA&refcode=em20260903-3966&amount=5&t=2&akid=3966%2E587540%2E6AimSn)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

clean_body: | The climate crisis knows no borders. That’s why we’re backing incredible champions everywhere — even in so-called red districts the Washington elite often shy away from. Meet Fred Clark and Jennifer Jenkins, two congressional candidates taking on uphill battles in Wisconsin and Florida to fight for a cleaner future: | 🟢 Fred Clark (WI-07) is a career conservationist and forester running to build out clean energy in rural Wisconsin. He’s a true climate champion we’d be so lucky to have in Washington, but here’s the catch: Fred’s opponent, Michael Alfonso, is endorsed by Trump, and he’s the son-in-law of Sean Duffy, Trump’s transportation secretary, who previously held this seat. Safe to say, Alfonso will have a whole lot of backing from the Republican money machine, so we’ve got to be ready. 🔵 Jennifer Jenkins (FL-08) is no stranger to tough fights. She flipped a school board seat in a district Trump won by 20 points – and now she’s running against a Trump-backed Republican who has taken money from Koch Industries, Chevron, and Big Pharma. Her district feels the direct harm of the climate crisis more than most. Hurricanes. Flooding. Increasing insurance costs. Jennifer has the ideas, and most importantly the backbone, to build Florida’s clean energy workforce and modernize infrastructure so working families are better prepared for the unimaginable. = We can't secure a liveable planet and future without backing leaders who will fight alongside us. This is the time to take bigger risks. And we need you with us. API PA is getting out the vote for our communities across the Commonwealth, and we are making sure that every voter feels confident casting their ballot early, by mail, or in-person on Election Day. Recently, mail voting has been in the news, and we want to clear up misinformation: **What’s happening?** The Trump administration is fighting to implement an [executive order](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138520793/644310501/1154225960?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9BVi9BVjAwMS8xLzgyNzA0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjVjNTMwNjA3LWNmYTctZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMjI0ODJhOTMzYiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=S6W3To0xFAc4NVsp71uYZiS12ZcTxL8bHsckalAi9wo=&emci=ac0597ee-fda6-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=5c530607-cfa7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=4069003) that would impact how the USPS delivers and processes mail-in ballots. Whistleblowers [report](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138520794/644310502/-480041093?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9BVi9BVjAwMS8xLzgyNzA0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjVjNTMwNjA3LWNmYTctZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMjI0ODJhOTMzYiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=S6W3To0xFAc4NVsp71uYZiS12ZcTxL8bHsckalAi9wo=&emci=ac0597ee-fda6-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=5c530607-cfa7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=4069003) that the USPS is scrambling to build a system to comply with the possible new rule in less than three months, and that the rush job could put votes in jeopardy. **This is an attempt to confuse voters and interfere with our elections.** The Trump administration’s fight to reform mail voting with just months to go is intentionally sloppy and confusing. They are trying to make voters second-guess themselves. **To be clear: Mail-in Voting hasn’t been affected.** The executive order is still being challenged in courts by dozens of states. All states have safeguarded, reliable policies in place to ensure vote-by-mail, and no USPS rule/regulation or executive order conflicts with them. Many states have adopted and supported vote-by-mail because it is a reliable way to participate in our free and democratic elections. Since voting by mail became available to everyone in Pennsylvania in 2020, tens of millions of ballots have been cast using this popular option. API PA is getting out the vote for our communities across the Commonwealth, and we are making sure that every voter feels confident casting their ballot early, by mail, or in-person on Election Day. The Trump administration is fighting to implement an that would impact how the USPS delivers and processes mail-in ballots. Whistleblowers that the USPS is scrambling to build a system to comply with the possible new rule in less than three months, and that the rush job could put votes in jeopardy. This is an attempt to confuse voters and interfere with our elections. The Trump administration’s fight to reform mail voting with just months to go is intentionally sloppy and confusing. They are trying to make voters second-guess themselves. To be clear: Mail-in Voting hasn’t been affected. The executive order is still being challenged in courts by dozens of states. All states have safeguarded, reliable policies in place to ensure vote-by-mail, and no USPS rule/regulation or executive order conflicts with them. Many states have adopted and supported vote-by-mail because it is a reliable way to participate in our free and democratic elections. Friends, Pennsylvania is one of the largest producers of fossil fuels in the country. **And right now, a climate champion is running to flip one of the most competitive districts in PA**. She plans to help families transition from expensive fossil fuels to cheaper renewables in order to **drive down their energy costs**. She wants to **fully fund SEPTA**. And she wants to **clean up orphaned natural gas wells**. Our grassroots fundraising isn’t where it needs to be right now, and we’ve had to drop our September projections.
At the same time as we’re falling behind, the GOP’s money, lies and attacks against me are ramping up. They’re pouring nearly $100 million so far into this race to defeat me – because if we lose in North Carolina, Democrats will have no shot at taking back the Senate.

The only way we can protect our narrow edge and keep powering forward is with a surge of grassroots support from people like you – so today, I’m trying something different. **I’m lowering my ask to just $1 in the hopes that every person reading this message chips in.**
While we have fundraising goals to hit, what matters most to me today is how many contributions we’re able to get in the door. Every dollar adds up fast when we’re all pitching in, and together, we can rebuild our momentum and show the strength of this grassroots movement.

Peter,

Sgt. Erik Duran dedicated 15 years of his life to the NYPD.He earned dozens of commendations. He helped take illegal guns off the streets. He put his life on the line to protect his community. Now he's fighting for his own freedom – All because of a split-second decision he made during a drug bust in the Bronx. | | | | | An undercover officer had just purchased narcotics from a suspect. As officers moved in to make the arrest, the suspect jumped on a motorized scooter and fled.Duran had only moments to react.He didn't reach for his firearm.He didn't use deadly force. Instead, he grabbed a nearby cooler and threw it into the suspect's path to stop him. The suspect crashed and later died from his injuries.Now, Sgt. Duran has been convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to prison.And he is fighting to clear his name through the appeals process. # [Detroit wants Congress to slam the door on Chinese dashboards](https://substack.com/redirect/0af80f08-c244-41ce-b423-d6bca3f8a678?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Detroit finally stopped whispering. The Alliance for Automotive Innovation told Congress Thursday to permanently ban the sale, import and manufacturing of Chinese connected vehicles, hardware and software before the session dies on Jan. 3. CEO John Bozzella called it dumping of subsidized connected cars. BYD and Geely already flood Europe and Latin America. Midterms hit in November.
* **Winners?** Detroit, the UAW, and every U.S. plant still standing. A statutory ban turns today's Commerce rule into law and keeps Chinese software out of American dashboards.
* **Losers?** BYD, Geely, **and Mercedes if the Senate bill treats nearly 20% Chinese ownership as a kill switch.** Europe and Latin America become the dumping ground.
* **Next?** Watch the Senate Commerce text before January. If Mercedes gets carved out, the ban is real. If not, lobbyists water it into another press release.

This is national-security cover for industrial policy, and I'm fine with that. China subsidizes the metal and owns the software. You don't let an adversary wire every car on I-95. Permanence beats another temporary Commerce rule. Congress either writes it into statute by Jan. 3 or spends 2027 explaining why it didn't.

Right now, almost every battery in America runs on lithium.
Your phone. Your laptop. Your car. Even the power grids storing clean energy.
But here's the catch: **China controls more than 70% of global lithium processing.**
That means America's future is tied to a supply chain we don't control. If China slows exports or raises prices...we're stuck.
Washington knows this can't continue. That's why, since January 2025, the White House has **signed or approved 160 mineral deals totaling nearly $40 billion.**
The goal: secure America's energy independence and cut China out of the equation. 1
This shift opens the door for a new winner.
Because while everyone else fights over lithium, one overlooked solution is ready right now... **sodium-ion batteries.**
Here's why they're a game changer:
* Sodium is **1,400x more abundant than lithium,** with significant reserves located in the U.S
* Batteries can be made at a **fraction of the cost of lithium -- up to 90% less expensive in the first year of use.**
* They last longer, are safer, and can be built at scale using domestic materials.

And one company is working to bring that solution to market: **Next Thing Technologies.**
Their batteries are being designed to scale from **massive grid storage projects** to **affordable $100/month home backup systems.**
That means they could power everything from America's infrastructure to your neighborhood.
The timing couldn't be better.
Billions in federal funding and private investment are flowing into U.S. mineral projects. Manufacturing is coming back home. And America is determined to break free from China's supply chains.
Next Thing Technologies is positioned to be the **backbone of this new energy era.**

# [Atkins just paved the Crypto onshore path Gensler spent four years blocking](https://substack.com/redirect/0af80f08-c244-41ce-b423-d6bca3f8a678?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
SEC Chairman Paul Atkins wants exemptions that put crypto capital raising back on U.S. soil. Regulation Crypto Assets would let startups raise $5 million over four years and larger issuers $75 million every 12 months, plus a safe harbor once the investment contract dies. The last crowd chased innovators offshore. Atkins wants the fees, listings, and tax base home.
* **Winners?** Onshore exchanges, token issuers, and U.S. listing banks. Clear exemptions beat four years of lawsuit-first regulation. Capital that fled Dubai and Singapore gets a reason to file here.
* **Losers?** Offshore venues that lived off the regulatory exile. Law-firm enforcement shops that billed hours instead of writing rules. Anyone still shorting "crypto is banned in America."
* **Next?** Public comment runs to Oct. 20, then a final rule. If CLARITY reaches Trump's desk, the statute and the SEC framework lock. If Congress stalls, Atkins moves anyway.

Capital goes where the rules are boring. Four years of enforcement-by-ambush shipped the industry overseas. Atkins is offering a path back under U.S. law. That's not charity. That's a bid to keep the fees, the listings, and the tax base onshore. Watch who files first once the comment window closes.

# [Tyson just admitted the cattle cycle is eating beef alive](https://substack.com/redirect/0af80f08-c244-41ce-b423-d6bca3f8a678?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Tyson Foods cut fiscal 2026 revenue growth to 1.5% to 2% from 2.5% to 3.5% and slashed adjusted operating income to $1.85 billion to $2.05 billion. Second cut in a month. Beef is now guided to lose $625 million to $775 million. CEO Donnie King blamed one of the most severe cattle shortages in U.S. history.
* **Winners?** Chicken and anyone selling cheaper protein. Tyson's chicken segment is still guided to $1.85 billion to $1.95 billion. Shoppers trade down. Ranchers with surviving herds print.
* **Losers?** Tyson shareholders and beef packers running oversized plants. The company is collapsing its beef network to three central facilities. TSN got smoked about 7% to $51.74.
* **Next?** Watch the Sept. 10 Barclays fireside. Relief only shows up when the herd rebuilds, and that is a fiscal 2027 story. Lower cattle prices just marked down the inventory.

You cannot will baby cattle into existence. Volatile prices plus a historic shortage left packers paying up, selling less, and writing down live inventories. Chicken is carrying the building. Beef is a hole. Until the U.S. herd turns, every guidance cut is just the cycle collecting rent.

# [Campbell's just confessed the pantry trade is broken](https://substack.com/redirect/0af80f08-c244-41ce-b423-d6bca3f8a678?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Campbell's slashed the quarterly dividend 36% to $0.25 from $0.39, or $1.00 annualized from $1.56, and called performance unacceptable. Fiscal 2026 sales fell 5% to $9.744 billion. Adjusted EPS dropped 27% to $2.17. Then they guided fiscal 2027 sales down another 2% to 4% and EPS to $1.65 to $1.80. CPB is getting crushed, down about 9%.
* **Winners?** Bondholders. The cut frees about $170 million a year for debt paydown. A new $500 million cost program by fiscal 2030 is for the balance sheet, not the brand.
* **Losers?** Income funds that bought soup for the yield. Snacks is the wound: Q4 organic sales -6%, operating earnings -34%, plus $117 million of Cape Cod and Kettle impairments.
* **Next?** More cuts before the $500 million shows up. Fiscal 2027 already assumes another down year. If snacks keep sliding, the next confession is asset sales.

subject: The Supreme Court is bending over backward to help Trump suppress voting rights

body:
Will you speak out alongside me today to condemn Trump’s assault on voting rights?
| | |
---
Friend, after its disastrous decision to gut the Voting Rights Act, Donald Trump’s Supreme Court has now paved a path for him to restrict your ability to vote by mail this November.
**And just this week, a whistleblower report revealed that Trump ordered the USPS to start using an unstable and untested system to handle mail-in ballots that could lead to significant issues as Georgians and Americans all across the country vote this fall.**
With the pivotal midterm elections quickly approaching, Trump and his allies are bending over backward to suppress the vote. At every turn, they are squeezing the voices of the people out of our democracy.
It’s all because they _know_ that they’ve taken your money through Trump’s tariffs. They _know_ they’ve taken your doctors and your healthcare. And they _know_ that you are rightfully outraged. So now, they’re trying to take your voice so you can’t hold them accountable at the ballot box.
**But let’s be clear: This is far from over. We will keep fighting this. With our very democracy at stake, we _must_.**
That’s why I’m counting on you to take action today and sign my brand-new petition to protect voting rights. **[Please, if you’re with me, will you add your name now to condemn Trump’s voter suppression efforts and protect the right to vote?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138524992/644319215/1367080036?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&ask=5&code=jtk5642-su-nd&refcode=jtk5642-su-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTEvMS85MDkwMSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0MTM2MmRlMS1kNGE3LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=qq8MahZr8nAGmtGOnimLV3hJ91BzdFGzHf4Ql_HD9Ls=&emci=b2bd4a53-e0a6-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=41362de1-d4a7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=1586379)**

clean_body: Will you speak out alongside me today to condemn Trump’s assault on voting rights? | | | Friend, after its disastrous decision to gut the Voting Rights Act, Donald Trump’s Supreme Court has now paved a path for him to restrict your ability to vote by mail this November. With the pivotal midterm elections quickly approaching, Trump and his allies are bending over backward to suppress the vote. At every turn, they are squeezing the voices of the people out of our democracy. It’s all because they know that they’ve taken your money through Trump’s tariffs. body:
| | | | Hi Friend,
Last week I stood on Ben's back porch in Ashburn, and I was shocked at what I saw.
I saw a data center built right up against his backyard and massive transmission lines obstructing the view of the community's lake. Ben showed me what unchecked growth has done to his community: a rising power bill, infrastructure nobody asked for running through his backyard, and an obstructed skyline.
---
[](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress.)
This didn't happen by accident. The person representing this district has had six years, in the House of Delegates, the State Senate, and now Congress, to do something about it. Suhas even admitted it himself: 10 years ago, he personally warned then-Congresswoman Barbara Comstock about the power lines, the utility bills, and the community impact, back when he worked at the White House on AI policy.
He knew. He just never acted on it. Six years later, all VA-10 has to show for it is a bill to study the problem further.
My goal is for Virginia to achieve energy independence through an all-of-the-above energy strategy, so we don't have to import power via transmission lines from neighboring states. And as for data centers: VA-10 has done its fair share in hosting. We can't keep putting this burden on our community.
Families like Ben's deserve a Representative who acts on what he knows, not someone who studies a problem for six years and starts talking about it once it's politically convenient.
_If you agree VA-10 deserves better, chip in $25, $50, or whatever you can right now, so we can get this message in front of every voter in this district before November 3rd._

God Bless, Dave Beckwith

#
This is Alexandria’s eighth back-to-school drive and we’re coming to you with an important ask:
As we wrap up hosting backpack and school supplies distributions throughout NY-14, [will you chip in $8 to help us fully cover the costs of this year’s backpack drive? Let us explain:](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260828-backpacks.sy4i40&refcode=em20260903-12225-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=12225%2E2526796%2EW3B8s4)
**We’re currently just over 50% of the way towards reaching our fundraising goal to fully cover the costs of this year’s back-to-school backpack drive.**
Every student should start the school year with the supplies they need to learn and grow.
Over the years, Alexandria has teamed up with NYC public housing developments, community organizations, and more to give thousands of kids a strong start to the school year with supplies and a backpack.
Initiatives like this one are only possible because of thousands of people chipping in what they can.
[ We’ve run the numbers and it costs our team $8-$10 to put together one backpack filled with school supplies. Can you chip in $8 today to help us reach our fundraising goal to fully cover the costs of this year’s backpack drive?](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260828-backpacks.sy4i40&refcode=em20260903-12225-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=12225%2E2526796%2EW3B8s4)
**[Contribute $8](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260828-backpacks.sy4i40&refcode=em20260903-12225-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=5&akid=12225%2E2526796%2EW3B8s4)**
Whether you can donate today or not, thank you for being here.
With gratitude,
Team AOC

The Supreme
Court just exposed how to get away with a racist map: call it politics.

In Louisiana v. Callais, a case about whether Louisiana's congressional
map illegally used race to cram voters of color into as few districts as
possible, the Supreme Court gave the green light for racial
gerrymandering... so long as you disguise it as political gerrymandering.

The Court handed lawmakers a script: call it partisan, and the
Constitution looks the other way. And the GOP didn’t wait to use it.

In Texas, the state supreme court ruled that a GOP-led county can redraw
its voting maps between the primary and the general election — mid-cycle,
after voters already know who's on the ballot.

That ruling exists because the U.S. Supreme Court cleared the path in
Callais.

This is what voter suppression looks like in 2026. Map lines redrawn by
extremist officials, mid-election, with the nation's highest court
standing guard instead of standing in the way. And it's not a one-off.
It's a pattern.

The Supreme Court is supposed to be independent. Instead, it keeps siding
with Trump, allowing him to cement his authoritarian agenda by any means
necessary, no matter the cost to the people.

With less than 9 weeks until Election Day, Trump and his cronies are
already interfering with what's supposed to be free and fair elections.
And the Supreme Court is letting them.

We're not staying silent. We're fighting back, mobilizing at the
grassroots level and building the public pressure to force real Court
reform, so Trump can no longer get away with schemes that serve no one but
himself.

We've known that as we get closer to Election Day, the polls will tighten and this race will heat up. But don't just take it from me.
Here's what CNN's election experts have to say about my campaign to flip this must-win U.S. Senate seat.
> #### "There's a real feeling... that this is a much tighter race than a lot of people nationally give it."
> #### "I think if you're a Democrat, don't sleep on this race, don't think it's automatically in the bag. You're gonna have to vote for it."
> #### "In this race, we had a Democratic former governor who has been a very popular governor over the years, but a lot of times that doesn't translate necessarily to a federal race... And so I think that's making this race a little bit closer."

| _**California was not broken
by accident.**_

But what's harsher is **a family getting priced out of the state they love** and watching billions get spent while the same problems get worse. | | |

name: Eric Schildge
subject: I know sheʼs feeling nervous.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Carleigh Beriont for Congress
body:
Because weʼre counting on her.

| |
---
| | Dear David, Carleighʼs final debate is tonight at 8pm on WMUR. Last week, she participated in a walkthrough of the debate stage along with the other candidates. Afterward, we went out for lunch, and I was surprised to see she didnʼt finish her cheeseburger. "Whatʼs the matter?" "Iʼm nervous," she said. "Youʼre nervous about the debate?" I asked, incredulous. How could she be? She was going to be amazing. "No," she said. "Iʼm nervous Iʼm going to win, and all these people are going to be counting on me." There are more than 700,000 people living in this district, and Carleigh knows exactly why sheʼs running: to go to Washington to try and fix the problems that make life so hard for regular people. Dear Fellow American, On behalf of all of us at Judicial Watch, I want to wish you and those close to you an enjoyable and relaxing **Labor Day** weekend. **I hope you have had a great summer!** The Judicial Watch team has been hard at **_work_** this summer fighting for clean elections, government accountability and against unconstitutional woke policies. _And our hard work is getting results thanks to your support_. **That’s why I want to ask you today to help keep this work fighting for the rule of law going!** | [KEEP THE MOMENTUM GOING ](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85140&L=37724&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL25kZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1NYXkmdXRtX3Rlcm09Tm9uLURvbm9ycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3e1e7ef2452949c706dc7caa9762525e05a0aa8699a2c23c9aad241394212ee7)

* **Our unprecedented voter-roll cleanup work,** which has led to the removal of **nearly 7 million** ineligible names nationwide, including **372,000** recently removed in **Colorado** , a settlement to review and remove **800,000** ineligible voter names in **Oregon** , and ongoing litigation against **California** and **Illinois** which could result in the _removal_ of an **_additional million dirty names_.**

* Defeating the city of Evanston's attempt to dismiss our constitutional challenge to its **race-based reparations program - **A _historic case_ which the **S. Department of Justice** has now filed to join.

* Securing a court order requiring the federal government to produce **nearly 2 million pages** of records discovered in a "hidden room" at the FBI.

* **A****landmark 7-2 Supreme Court victory** this spring affirming the right of federal candidates to challenge election rules in court;

We are now pivoting into a very busy fall where _we must prepare_ for the very real prospect of a _Leftist takeover_ of the House and Senate and a **growing communist influence** in Congress. With congressional oversight in the hands of the far Left, your **Judicial Watch** could remain the **only game in town** for holding Deep State actors _accountable_ , _fighting back_ against the Left's lawfare machine, and _upholding_ constitution liberties. **Every Judicial Watch investigation, record request, and legal action comes with major costs against opponents with deep pockets (often funded by the Soros network).** But, with _[your continued financial backing](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85140&L=37724&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL25kZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1NYXkmdXRtX3Rlcm09Tm9uLURvbm9ycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3e1e7ef2452949c706dc7caa9762525e05a0aa8699a2c23c9aad241394212ee7)_ , Judicial Watch will continue to file lawsuits wherever the rule of law is threatened, and I'm confident I'll be able to keep sending you victory updates like this in the near future. _[Will you honor our team's hard work and commitment to the rule of law with a special gift today](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85140&L=37724&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL25kZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1NYXkmdXRtX3Rlcm09Tm9uLURvbm9ycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3e1e7ef2452949c706dc7caa9762525e05a0aa8699a2c23c9aad241394212ee7)_? | [YES, I'LL HELP JUDICIAL WATCH FIGHT AND WIN< ](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85140&L=37724&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL25kZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1NYXkmdXRtX3Rlcm09Tm9uLURvbm9ycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3e1e7ef2452949c706dc7caa9762525e05a0aa8699a2c23c9aad241394212ee7)

Friends,
On Saturday, we had the honor of having the CEO of Planned Parenthood Federation of America, Alexis McGill Johnson, join us on the campaign trail as we traveled all across the district.
Under the Trump Administration, enabled by our own Congressman Mike Lawler, we are watching a war being waged against women’s healthcare. Last year, Lawler cast the deciding vote for the One Big Ugly Bill, gutting healthcare access nationwide and leaving organizations like Planned Parenthood unable to provide family planning, abortion care, STI testing, cancer screening, and other lifesaving services that millions of people rely on.

If I have the honor of being your next representative in Congress, I promise to fight like hell alongside incredible groups like the Hudson Valley’s own Choice Matters, to codify Roe v. Wade, protect and expand access to affordable healthcare, and restore federal funding to Planned Parenthood. This is a dark chapter in our country’s history. But we have to keep fighting, because the next generation deserves to grow up in an America that protects our rights and actually delivers on its promises.
With gratitude and fire, Cait Conley

Under the Trump Administration, enabled by our own Congressman Mike Lawler, we are watching a war being waged against women’s healthcare. Last year, Lawler cast the deciding vote for the One Big Ugly Bill, gutting healthcare access nationwide and leaving organizations like Planned Parenthood unable to provide family planning, abortion care, STI testing, cancer screening, and other lifesaving services that millions of people rely on. If I have the honor of being your next representative in Congress, I promise to fight like hell alongside incredible groups like the Hudson Valley’s own Choice Matters, to codify Roe v. Wade, protect and expand access to affordable healthcare, and restore federal funding to Planned Parenthood. This is a dark chapter in our country’s history. But we have to keep fighting, because the next generation deserves to grow up in an America that protects our rights and actually delivers on its promises. name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: AIPAC and their donors have one goal
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
The bad news is we are not always going to be able to out-raise AIPAC. But the good news is we don’t need to.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260903-6680-footer&t=1&akid=6680%2E420207%2E5dYj5h)
Peter,
**AIPAC has already spent more than $100 million this election cycle. And we still have two months to go until Election Day.**
[**If that’s all you need to hear, will you chip in $3 right now to help me fight back and support progressive candidates across the country?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260903.kiRObD&refcode=em20260903-6680&amount=3&t=2&akid=6680%2E420207%2E5dYj5h)
Their right-wing billionaire donors have one goal: to defeat progressive candidates and _anyone_ who dares speak out against the genocide that the Israeli military is committing against Palestinians.
They spent $30 million opposing Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan. They opposed Daniel Biss in Illinois. They came after my sister Susheela in Oregon, and they’ve come after me in the past, too (they’re even staffing up right here in Seattle as we speak).
The bad news is we are not always going to be able to out-raise AIPAC. _But the good news is we don’t need to._
Abdul won in Michigan. Daniel won in Illinois. Working people have already proved that we can come together, organize, and beat AIPAC’s money at the ballot box.
**We have something that AIPAC doesn’t: millions of people across this country who share our progressive values, believe in justice, and know that our government shouldn’t be up for sale to the highest bidder.**
So while we don’t need to match them dollar for dollar, we _do_ need the resources to run winning campaigns. It takes money to organize, knock on doors, make calls, get our message out, and fight back against right-wing attacks.
And since I don’t take a dime from corporate PACs, grassroots donors like you are absolutely essential to funding everything we do.
[**Peter, if you’re with me, can I count on you to pitch in $3 or any amount today to help me keep up this critical work on behalf of our movement?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260903.kiRObD&refcode=em20260903-6680&amount=3&t=3&akid=6680%2E420207%2E5dYj5h)
**[Contribute $3](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260903.kiRObD&amount=3&refcode=em20260903-6680&t=22&akid=6680%2E420207%2E5dYj5h)**
Together, we can prove that people power is stronger than any amount of money billionaires can spend. But only if we come together and take action.
In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal
**[Contribute](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-footer?refcode=em20260903-6680-footer&t=23&refcode2=6680_420207_5dYj5h&akid=6680%2E420207%2E5dYj5h)**

**Protesting poll closures in Tarrant County** ** ** **TOP, partner organizations, and voting rights advocates were out in force Tuesday in downtown Fort Worth, holding a People's Mic event** to protest the Republican-controlled Tarrant County Commissioners Court voting to close 92 polling places ahead of the midterm. [_**Read about it in the Texas Tribune.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138528353/644329363/737407205?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNVE8vMS80NTY0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhYzNiYjliOS1kZWE3LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=sOhz1sTMcG9EHUL5ZCvXwfsvLiI8RnpOXoUDY-HAFT4=&emci=61a0afc6-cda7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=ac3bb9b9-dea7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=227997) Despite what Tarrant County's MAGA county judge Tim O'Hare would have us believe, cutting dozens of polling places in predominantly Black and Latino parts of the county just weeks before a major election has nothing to do with administrative costs, **and EVERYTHING to do with suppressing votes.** It's the clearest sign yet that Tarrant County GOP leaders have no desire on winning over votes and instead shamelessly choose to silence entire communities. [_**Like and share this Facebook video of TOP’s Executive Director Brianna Brown slamming this political move.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138528354/644329365/327485576?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNVE8vMS80NTY0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhYzNiYjliOS1kZWE3LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=sOhz1sTMcG9EHUL5ZCvXwfsvLiI8RnpOXoUDY-HAFT4=&emci=61a0afc6-cda7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=ac3bb9b9-dea7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=227997) For decades, Texas has been ground zero in voter suppression efforts. TOP firmly believes elected leaders should be doing everything in their power to expand the electorate, not shrink it. **Help us take a stand for fair voting access by pitching in below.** [****](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138528356/644329366/1730099438?refcode=9.3.26NL&amount=25.00&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNVE8vMS80NTY0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhYzNiYjliOS1kZWE3LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=sOhz1sTMcG9EHUL5ZCvXwfsvLiI8RnpOXoUDY-HAFT4=)

Tiffany is a true public servant. She doesn’t take any money from corporate PACs, and she’s running for re-election to**keep fighting for:**
* equitable public school funding
* dignity and protection for students who are LGBTQ+, immigrants, and/or in foster care
* increased literacy for all, including English language learners
* more career and technical education to expand pathways to good-paying jobs
* mental health and substance abuse prevention services for students
* support for educators and struggling families
* safe schools where every child matters, belongs, and thrives

Tiffany works with students who refuse to give up, even when the odds are stacked against them.
She’s been one of those students. She knows what it’s like to be unheard and to navigate systems that weren’t built for her.

When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance.

Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity.

Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find.

So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families.

And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying nearly 20 bucks for a gallon of fuel. They don’t even believe us.

They're focused on their own wallets – not ours.

And when they actually work together on something, it’s usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest.

It’s why our prices keep rising, all while the healthcare and services Alaskans rely on get gutted.

I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home.

My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning.

But if we’re going to secure Alaska’s future, we need another priority: fighting corruption.

I'm running for Alaska's Senate seat because it is the fight for our future.
