An Ittihad Deir al-Balah football player jumps over an agility ladder in a training session ahead of the Thousand Martyrs Cup. August 2026. Courtesy of Ittihad Deir al-Balah.
On a dirt field in the dense coastal neighborhood of Deir al-Balah last week, players from Ittihad Deir al-Balah--one of Gaza's three standing football clubs--gathered their torn balls, scuffed training cones, and rusted equipment. Surrounded by rubble and with Israeli drones buzzing overhead, they were preparing to train for a football tournament, the first in Palestine since 2023.
Last month, the Palestinian Football Association (PFA) announced the return of football to clubs across Palestine and Lebanon after a three-year hiatus marked by Israel's genocide in Gaza, terrorism in the occupied West Bank, and a brutal war on Lebanon. The resumption of the football association's leagues in Gaza, the West Bank, Jerusalem, and Palestinian refugee camps in Lebanon will open on September 4 with the Thousand Martyrs Cup, a two-month tournament named for the more than 1,000 Palestinian athletes killed by Israel since October 7, 2023.
Over 240 clubs are participating in the tournament: 50 clubs in Gaza, 165 in the West Bank and Jerusalem, and 28 clubs in Lebanon. Opening games will simultaneously kick off at 6 p.m. Jerusalem Time on Friday. Matches in Gaza will be played on four chewed-up artificial turf five-a-side football courts, including Ittihad Deir al-Balah's playground. In the West Bank, Jerusalem, and Lebanon, the matches will be played on standard eleven-a-side pitches.
Players and coaches told Drop Site News they have mixed feelings about the resumption of Palestinian football, with Israel's violence making life all but impossible, while at the same time wanting to pay tribute to the martyrs and stand resilient.
Yet it is unclear if players in Gaza will be able to even show up to the tournament, the assistant coach of Ittihad Deir al-Balah, Motaz Rabia, told Drop Site News. He said the continued daily Israeli airstrikes and relentless attacks have forced the team's training sessions to be cancelled and have restricted players' movement.
Just last week, Israeli fighter jets bombed the neighbourhood adjacent to the club building in Deir al-Balah as well as the Abu-Salim Mosque downtown. On Saturday, an Israeli airstrike on a motorcycle in the Jabaliya refugee camp in northern Gaza killed Khadamat Jabaliya club star Abdel-Fattah Abu-Aish, less than a week before the tournament.
Every club in Gaza has suffered tremendous losses. Ittihad Deir al-Balah alone lost at least ten players, staffers, and coaches in Israeli attacks, including Asian Football Confederation-approved manager Hani Al-Mosadar and star midfielder Nasrallah Al-Mqataa. Other players have been forced to quit football to try and provide bare life essentials for their families.
At least 1,013 athletes have been killed by Israel in Gaza and the West Bank since October 2023, according to the PFA, including nearly 570 footballers, over 100 of them children. The Israeli military has also destroyed or damaged nearly 270 sports facilities in Gaza, including nine out of 10 stadiums and 51 out of 54 club facilities.
The PFA spokesperson in Gaza, Mustafa Siyam, told Drop Site he hopes the tournament will restore "some semblance of normalcy" for Gaza's footballers and mark the "start of a new chapter" for football in the devastated enclave.
In Gaza, a historically intense derby between Khadamat Rafah and Shabab Rafah will kick off the Thousand Martyrs Tournament: Two rivals from a once-vibrant city, now razed and occupied by Israeli forces. Meanwhile, Jabal Al-Mokaber will play against Shabab Al-Khalil in the opening match in the West Bank. Al-Ansar will take on Al-Nahda in Lebanon.
"Despite Israel's deliberate targeting of athletes and ban on the entry of football equipment, we are very keen on reviving football activities for our players," Siyam said. "This tournament carries many messages, especially since it bears the names of our very dear players who were killed during the genocide. It also holds out hope for a better future for football in Gaza."
## **" Israel blocks footballs"**
The Ittihad Deir al-Balah football club has barely been able to hold training sessions once or twice a week ahead of the tournament, and scarcely has any equipment to function with daily Israeli airstrikes and an ongoing crippling siege, according to Rabia.
"We can't afford a training ball. Israel blocks footballs. One flat ball now costs around $400. Our players can't afford the food to rebuild their fitness and physicality. We're very reluctant to participate, but we're playing to honor our martyred players and staffers," Rabia told Drop Site. "We have players now displaced in the southernmost part of Gaza. We can't even cover their transportation fees and bring them to play. Therefore, we have called up the youths."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2b4e631d-f0f0-4c4e-9e89-7d333f62e24b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Ittihad Deir al-Balah assistant coach Motaz Rabia (right) next to the club's manager in a training session before the the Thousand Martyrs Cup. August 2026. Courtesy of Ittihad Deir al-Balah.
Rabia said that football means a lot to everyone at the club and that their continued involvement is emblematic of their steadfastness.
"Sports unite people. In Gaza, football has died. We have so much talent and potential for the world, but we are completely shrugged off. I hope FIFA listens to us and treats us as human beings. We deserve to be seen and take our chances," he lamented.
"All we want to see in Gaza now is an actual ceasefire because it doesn't exist," he added. "I wish to wake up one day without more bombings and casualties. And we hope to see justice in this world where basic human rights and rules apply to all, including Palestinians."
Under its president Gianni Infantino, FIFA controversially took part in President Donald Trump's so-called Board of Peace, which has been tasked with overseeing Gaza, and pledged to reconstruct Gaza's football infrastructure through a $75 million plan announced at the inaugural meeting in February. There has been zero progress on the plan so far.
Siyam, the PFA spokesperson, told Drop Site that the association was not informed of the details of the alleged FIFA plan but said any support was "welcome" and urged FIFA to expedite it.
Meanwhile, Israel has routinely violated the "ceasefire" that went into effect in October 2025, killing over 1,300 Palestinians and wounding over 4,400, according to Gaza's Health Ministry, while severely restricting the entry of life essentials, humanitarian aid, medical supplies, and reconstruction materials and equipment. The Israeli military has also continued to encroach on Palestinian land, pushing the "yellow line" that demarcates its line of control further westward where it now occupies nearly 70% of the Gaza Strip.
## **" I may be killed in the next 15 minutes"**
Mohammed Al-Taramasi, 26, who plays right back for Shabab Jabaliya Club and Palestine's Olympic Team, lives in a dilapidated tent in the Jabaliya refugee camp close to the "yellow line" where he is forced to survive daily artillery shelling, shooting, and attacks from tanks and quadcopters from Israeli troops nearby.
Al-Taramasi was displaced from his home nearly three years ago when Israeli warplanes carpet bombed his neighborhood in the camp on October 28, 2023, killing his father and dozens of extended family members. He somehow survived the attack and buried his father, whom he described as "his backbone".
"I used to wake up for my training. Now, gunshots terrify my family and me in the morning," Al-Taramasi told Drop Site. "I am now talking to you on the phone and I may be killed in the next 15 minutes. My father was killed. I am displaced. I missed out on offers from Egypt and Libya in 2024 because I couldn't leave Gaza. My life resembles hell on earth," he said, choking up with grief and sorrow.
"There are two sides of the tournament: positive and negative," he continued. "Positive because it is a tribute to our colleagues on the football stage. Negative because we're not getting paid enough and the cup may have to be called off. It's a nerve-wracking situation for all of us. But I wish to lift the trophy for the sake of the slain footballers and my teammates and neighbors."
Al-Taramasi said he hopes international football bodies and media outlets would focus more on the plight of Gaza's football players and that many of them have the potential to embark on stellar careers if only they were given the same attention as players abroad.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/02eb6672-df70-44f9-a617-bf3bcb477f8b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Players from Ittihad Deir al-Balah football club train on a dirt playground ahead of the Thousand Martyrs Cup. August 2026. Courtesy of Ittihad Deir al-Balah.
Outside of Palestine, Palestinian footballers living in exile also face enormous challenges. Palestinian playmaker and winger Mohammed Hamada, 25, plays for Al-Okhwa Club in the Saida refugee camp in Lebanon. Hamada's grandparents were forced from their home in Acre, on the northern coastline of historic Palestine, during the Nakba in 1948. Palestinian refugees in Lebanon are unable to return to or visit any part of Palestine, since Lebanon-approved travel documents are not recognized by Israeli authorities and they cannot apply for a visa to enter the Occupied Territories.
Similar to Palestinian athletes in Gaza and the West Bank who are denied permits by Israel to travel, Mohammed has had opportunities to play abroad, but his precarious status in Lebanon with no passport and only a travel document left him unable to pursue his dreams. Ahead of the tournament on Friday, he says this cup means more than anything to him and he is eager to play in honor of his people in Gaza.
"I can't enter Palestine. I have been heartbroken by what has been happening during the last three years. Playing in this tournament is so emotionally overwhelming that I can't put it into words," he said in a quavering voice. "I am determined to win the trophy to pay the finest tribute to the thousand martyrs. This tournament will offer us a chance to convey our message as football players, and football is a great avenue for speaking up."
"I hope the world looks more at Gaza and Palestine," he added. "It's enough of what has already transpired. I want all the international support, particularly from FIFA and football associations, to go to the players in Gaza and Palestine. We all failed Gaza, no matter what we do."

August 2026. Courtesy of Ittihad Deir al-Balah. On a dirt field in the dense coastal neighborhood of Deir al-Balah last week, players from Ittihad Deir al-Balah--one of Gaza's three standing football clubs--gathered their torn balls, scuffed training cones, and rusted equipment. Surrounded by rubble and with Israeli drones buzzing overhead, they were preparing to train for a football tournament, the first in Palestine since 2023. Last month, the Palestinian Football Association (PFA) announced the return of football to clubs across Palestine and Lebanon after a three-year hiatus marked by Israel's genocide in Gaza, terrorism in the occupied West Bank, and a brutal war on Lebanon. The resumption of the football association's leagues in Gaza, the West Bank, Jerusalem, and Palestinian refugee camps in Lebanon will open on September 4 with the Thousand Martyrs Cup, a two-month tournament named for the more than 1,000 Palestinian athletes killed by Israel since October 7, 2023. Over 240 clubs are participating in the tournament: 50 clubs in Gaza, 165 in the West Bank and Jerusalem, and 28 clubs in Lebanon. Opening games will simultaneously kick off at 6 p.m. Jerusalem Time on Friday. Matches in Gaza will be played on four chewed-up artificial turf five-a-side football courts, including Ittihad Deir al-Balah's playground. In the West Bank, Jerusalem, and Lebanon, the matches will be played on standard eleven-a-side pitches. Players and coaches told Drop Site News they have mixed feelings about the resumption of Palestinian football, with Israel's violence making life all but impossible, while at the same time wanting to pay tribute to the martyrs and stand resilient. Yet it is unclear if players in Gaza will be able to even show up to the tournament, the assistant coach of Ittihad Deir al-Balah, Motaz Rabia, told Drop Site News. He said the continued daily Israeli airstrikes and relentless attacks have forced the team's training sessions to be cancelled and have restricted players' movement. Just last week, Israeli fighter jets bombed the neighbourhood adjacent to the club building in Deir al-Balah as well as the Abu-Salim Mosque downtown. On Saturday, an Israeli airstrike on a motorcycle in the Jabaliya refugee camp in northern Gaza killed Khadamat Jabaliya club star Abdel-Fattah Abu-Aish, less than a week before the tournament. Every club in Gaza has suffered tremendous losses. Ittihad Deir al-Balah alone lost at least ten players, staffers, and coaches in Israeli attacks, including Asian Football Confederation-approved manager Hani Al-Mosadar and star midfielder Nasrallah Al-Mqataa. Other players have been forced to quit football to try and provide bare life essentials for their families. At least 1,013 athletes have been killed by Israel in Gaza and the West Bank since October 2023, according to the PFA, including nearly 570 footballers, over 100 of them children. The Israeli military has also destroyed or damaged nearly 270 sports facilities in Gaza, including nine out of 10 stadiums and 51 out of 54 club facilities. The PFA spokesperson in Gaza, Mustafa Siyam, told Drop Site he hopes the tournament will restore "some semblance of normalcy" for Gaza's footballers and mark the "start of a new chapter" for football in the devastated enclave. In Gaza, a historically intense derby between Khadamat Rafah and Shabab Rafah will kick off the Thousand Martyrs Tournament: Two rivals from a once-vibrant city, now razed and occupied by Israeli forces. Meanwhile, Jabal Al-Mokaber will play against Shabab Al-Khalil in the opening match in the West Bank. Al-Ansar will take on Al-Nahda in Lebanon. "Despite Israel's deliberate targeting of athletes and ban on the entry of football equipment, we are very keen on reviving football activities for our players," Siyam said. "This tournament carries many messages, especially since it bears the names of our very dear players who were killed during the genocide. It also holds out hope for a better future for football in Gaza." " Israel blocks footballs" The Ittihad Deir al-Balah football club has barely been able to hold training sessions once or twice a week ahead of the tournament, and scarcely has any equipment to function with daily Israeli airstrikes and an ongoing crippling siege, according to Rabia. "We can't afford a training ball. Israel blocks footballs. One flat ball now costs around $400. Our players can't afford the food to rebuild their fitness and physicality. We're very reluctant to participate, but we're playing to honor our martyred players and staffers," Rabia told Drop Site. "We have players now displaced in the southernmost part of Gaza. We can't even cover their transportation fees and bring them to play. Therefore, we have called up the youths." | | ---|---|--- Ittihad Deir al-Balah assistant coach Motaz Rabia (right) next to the club's manager in a training session before the the Thousand Martyrs Cup. August 2026. Courtesy of Ittihad Deir al-Balah. Rabia said that football means a lot to everyone at the club and that their continued involvement is emblematic of their steadfastness. "Sports unite people. In Gaza, football has died. We have so much talent and potential for the world, but we are completely shrugged off. I hope FIFA listens to us and treats us as human beings. We deserve to be seen and take our chances," he lamented. "All we want to see in Gaza now is an actual ceasefire because it doesn't exist," he added. "I wish to wake up one day without more bombings and casualties. And we hope to see justice in this world where basic human rights and rules apply to all, including Palestinians." Under its president Gianni Infantino, FIFA controversially took part in President Donald Trump's so-called Board of Peace, which has been tasked with overseeing Gaza, and pledged to reconstruct Gaza's football infrastructure through a $75 million plan announced at the inaugural meeting in February. There has been zero progress on the plan so far. Siyam, the PFA spokesperson, told Drop Site that the association was not informed of the details of the alleged FIFA plan but said any support was "welcome" and urged FIFA to expedite it. Meanwhile, Israel has routinely violated the "ceasefire" that went into effect in October 2025, killing over 1,300 Palestinians and wounding over 4,400, according to Gaza's Health Ministry, while severely restricting the entry of life essentials, humanitarian aid, medical supplies, and reconstruction materials and equipment. The Israeli military has also continued to encroach on Palestinian land, pushing the "yellow line" that demarcates its line of control further westward where it now occupies nearly 70% of the Gaza Strip. " I may be killed in the next 15 minutes" Mohammed Al-Taramasi, 26, who plays right back for Shabab Jabaliya Club and Palestine's Olympic Team, lives in a dilapidated tent in the Jabaliya refugee camp close to the "yellow line" where he is forced to survive daily artillery shelling, shooting, and attacks from tanks and quadcopters from Israeli troops nearby. Al-Taramasi was displaced from his home nearly three years ago when Israeli warplanes carpet bombed his neighborhood in the camp on October 28, 2023, killing his father and dozens of extended family members. He somehow survived the attack and buried his father, whom he described as "his backbone". "I used to wake up for my training. Now, gunshots terrify my family and me in the morning," Al-Taramasi told Drop Site. "I am now talking to you on the phone and I may be killed in the next 15 minutes. My father was killed. I am displaced. I missed out on offers from Egypt and Libya in 2024 because I couldn't leave Gaza. My life resembles hell on earth," he said, choking up with grief and sorrow. "There are two sides of the tournament: positive and negative," he continued. "Positive because it is a tribute to our colleagues on the football stage. Negative because we're not getting paid enough and the cup may have to be called off. It's a nerve-wracking situation for all of us. But I wish to lift the trophy for the sake of the slain footballers and my teammates and neighbors." Al-Taramasi said he hopes international football bodies and media outlets would focus more on the plight of Gaza's football players and that many of them have the potential to embark on stellar careers if only they were given the same attention as players abroad. | | ---|---|--- Players from Ittihad Deir al-Balah football club train on a dirt playground ahead of the Thousand Martyrs Cup. August 2026. Courtesy of Ittihad Deir al-Balah. Outside of Palestine, Palestinian footballers living in exile also face enormous challenges. Palestinian playmaker and winger Mohammed Hamada, 25, plays for Al-Okhwa Club in the Saida refugee camp in Lebanon. Hamada's grandparents were forced from their home in Acre, on the northern coastline of historic Palestine, during the Nakba in 1948. Palestinian refugees in Lebanon are unable to return to or visit any part of Palestine, since Lebanon-approved travel documents are not recognized by Israeli authorities and they cannot apply for a visa to enter the Occupied Territories. Similar to Palestinian athletes in Gaza and the West Bank who are denied permits by Israel to travel, Mohammed has had opportunities to play abroad, but his precarious status in Lebanon with no passport and only a travel document left him unable to pursue his dreams. Ahead of the tournament on Friday, he says this cup means more than anything to him and he is eager to play in honor of his people in Gaza. "I can't enter Palestine. I have been heartbroken by what has been happening during the last three years. Playing in this tournament is so emotionally overwhelming that I can't put it into words," he said in a quavering voice. "I am determined to win the trophy to pay the finest tribute to the thousand martyrs. This tournament will offer us a chance to convey our message as football players, and football is a great avenue for speaking up." "I hope the world looks more at Gaza and Palestine," he added. name: Save the Persecuted Christians
subject: An unholy alliance is building
body:
There is an unholy alliance forming in America that should not be possible.

| | | | | |
---
[ ](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=19bb697786954a2db72fe900648e4245&_e=WzahAEu1eclIGTLsigQA8fFaUCAK5DuwC6Xmk_ClvmndiqQSGHfjyOuflDKd8EhPvVBn9gIKtRLwG2fXMqmRE8u27ZmnYkIGKfBOglpbBpVV7B_W4jNHJRAytp9A9jP9AC1zB-yC6gbVQRB6DDq2HXXc9vBCQSCs4Iwzy_sX2w9FE0x7pYr7YIvUc4nIFtNo19EYwMizUwRmedFxo5p2-JbENHXVi1HX0PoseuYNnpVYLF64nB7D7xglum5DtOzuckZ37-sgX-Zu3sHzzPd-_cchwk4PqLNKOk4Dsfrs-HJ4I-0OiU6e-aMGkiYDKcDke43gUirCvrWHRYkF_kG8OivQMsASiw7UTiCUmeo6KDT_PnyXNC3b-VtTi6KEy6L-P5pJgijjqGD5gyn6LlkNXIgDhbxFdOZB8bTU2CFSd0J8hMIhW2umCUxyD4BylpeBHq5_ALHWHqtfnJeWYgIAxUE03-z5yJNXmCd2VLIwq_l8XUOF9sDO3cs3aMia2mosL57VjYdniH3gSkaZoOfUJ8Z1RQbViX-882eiqJ-XEFPeDimVYVov0NaimJytR-Up)
---
|
---
| | Dear Friend,
There is an unholy alliance forming in America that should not be possible.
**On one side stand revolutionary socialists who believe there is no God at all** – and that America will not be free until every trace of its Judeo-Christian foundation is scrubbed out of our schools, our courts, and our public life.
**On the other stand political Islamists who believe their god must rule** every one of those things absolutely, and that no other faith has any rightful claim to exist beside it.
They disagree about the most fundamental question a human being can ask – _and yet they have found each other._
**Because they have found the same enemy.**
That enemy is not a political party. It is not a candidate. **It is the Christian faith** – the last thing standing between both of these movements and the world they intend to build.
---
[ ](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=19bb697786954a2db72fe900648e4245&_e=WzahAEu1eclIGTLsigQA8fFaUCAK5DuwC6Xmk_ClvmndiqQSGHfjyOuflDKd8EhPvVBn9gIKtRLwG2fXMqmRE8u27ZmnYkIGKfBOglpbBpVV7B_W4jNHJRAytp9A9jP9AC1zB-yC6gbVQRB6DDq2HXXc9vBCQSCs4Iwzy_sX2w9FE0x7pYr7YIvUc4nIFtNo852lnzxObhOJJEiEHc526LzHwZv96xxmEI5YEr3ZZc_mqm_oDyozfk2s2FNMcNhUyddVyutjsJfuz9laM3MOb9HLxb_TlkFjrayuU-GT17_n7ozTi16mDMSLI4vaM-pkOlA1VIaTrTrr12OQf21P29C_QtRedE3mONib_MRcR5t_PssnHDWMOyDTuTDrs0VcLtrH1ChCVMk9Z2VkpJhVXlv2UobRIOOlU1ehnf3HKvyBqOVdzEOOrVt-UiYca6Dx7q98JNXCyb4nanbCa5B0R78wMgnmqXMUJi1yj9GXLARH5n7AwVedWDEm_rhY7_XqmLX_23c9t4Qty2_tDZCcan-CudBvIw3XgtMvKrvGdFPxIc5Tmq3t1nqtGFWHJRAY)
---
President Trump named the first threat plainly:
"These ruthless communists will attack all religions, but in particular Christianity. They always do. They're after Christianity more than any other religion."
He is right, and history proves it. Every communist revolution of the last century began by locking the church doors. In China, _Pastor Ezra Jin spent 266 days in prison_ for leading one of the country's largest underground churches. Eight of his fellow pastors are still behind bars. In North Korea, _owning a Bible can cost you the rest of your life in a labor camp._
Secretary of State Marco Rubio named the second:
"Radical Islam isn't content with controlling a single region or establishing a small caliphate. Its ideology is revolutionary. It aims to grow, to dominate, and to exert control over more lands and more populations."
That is the whole project of political Islam: **placing religious power above every constitution, every court, and every conscience. **There is no room left in it for religious liberty. No room for a man to read the Gospel and decide for himself that it is true.
And if you want to know what that project does to a man who decides exactly that, consider Nissar Hussain.
---
[ ](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=19bb697786954a2db72fe900648e4245&_e=WzahAEu1eclIGTLsigQA8fFaUCAK5DuwC6Xmk_ClvmndiqQSGHfjyOuflDKd8EhPvVBn9gIKtRLwG2fXMqmRE8u27ZmnYkIGKfBOglpbBpVV7B_W4jNHJRAytp9A9jP9AC1zB-yC6gbVQRB6DDq2HXXc9vBCQSCs4Iwzy_sX2w9FE0x7pYr7YIvUc4nIFtNoYUOB7vOj6BfJdTWzsrce7gskK9Nd_LpDvqz5JmHRNLPkGJDv0lFKUwiOFsYtsP4QeD8hPm5EvKt-uwsTAeDUgg6PumvEOBz8OZUkQhUQPweSc6ynr8VyrYwQhw9ebpAEl2LAW0H3OERr6d6KJFwbhUolspebxSTM4UbQeIRKFgRhKKGqEaJ6gt9HBd8pvL_069CpgYq1Ooq160diEBbj4EIXt7UPjZWMkNLqgTcgt3u4h3DoQw8zNWNL_LJTmfTPoTsCnfMwWCQE0Hu7DvZo6WCyi9Ms60cn1ciu14AdwWzFQ_KSeEeTLrKMjPtXynCJyBg1S9y7tgJiK8y64RNHJ3dvtABtDVGp5TlCYK2EPZpsujzYJCtuWMldAAd4Vdvu)
---
Nissar left Islam and gave his life to Jesus Christ. For that, he spent seventeen years being hunted. Not in Tehran. Not in Nigeria. _In Bradford, England._
His kneecap was shattered in an attack outside his own home. His car was set on fire. His children were taunted in the street as "infidels." His family lived under police protection for nearly a decade.
_Not one bishop of the Church of England stood with him._
Nissar's "crime" carries a death sentence in eleven nations on this earth.
Now look at what happens where this ideology governs without restraint.
**In Nigeria, more than 100,000 Christians have been massacred since 2009. 19,000 churches burned or destroyed. Five million men, women, and children driven from their homes. **
This is not history. _It is now._
Just before midnight on July 26, militants entered the village of Naridon and went house to house, shooting. **Thirty Christians were killed. Eleven were children. The youngest was three years old.**
On August 1, thousands gathered for a single funeral Mass. _Twenty-seven caskets._
That is not a distant tragedy. That is the destination.
**And that ideology now has political sponsorship inside the United States – with a partner supplying it lawyers, funding, and votes.**
**Start in Dearborn, Michigan.**
Pastor Lorenzo Sewell prayed at President Trump's inauguration. Today he says Christians there come to him quietly, from every corner of the city, with the same message: "I'm with you, but I'm afraid to say it."
**Afraid to say they follow Christ.** _**In America.** _
Sewell describes a city where the call to prayer is broadcast over loudspeakers, where the public schools certify that every ounce of meat served to children is prepared according to Islamic ritual law, and where his own wife's life was threatened – the man's name and address handed to police – and nothing happened.
"Think about being in a Christian nation," he said, "being afraid to talk about Christ."
**Then look at our schools.**
At two of the top public high schools in Virginia, students filmed promotional videos for their Muslim student clubs showing classmates hooded, dragged away, and thrown into car trunks – weeks after the anniversary of the October 7th massacre. The district disciplined them. Congress opened an investigation. And then a national Islamic advocacy group hauled the school system into federal court, _arguing that punishing the students was itself discrimination._
The provocation comes from one side. The lawyers come from the other.
**Then look at New York City.**
_The largest city in America is now run by a self-described Democratic Socialist who took his oath of office on the Quran_ – elected with six figures of help from a network of Islamist organizations, including one whose leaders have been tied to terror-financing investigations. It's why he can visit a mosque in the morning and march in an LGBTQ parade that afternoon.
The socialists supply the political machine and the moral cover. The Islamists supply the ideology and the money. Neither could do this alone. _Together, they are formidable. _
**"If the world hates you, keep in mind that it hated me first."** – John 15:18
Jesus told us this would come. He did not tell us to be silent about it.
**This is precisely why Save the Persecuted Christians exists. We guide a coalition of over 200 organizations fighting this battle on both fronts at once – because they are the same battle.**
✅ We brought Nissar Hussain to America and put him before members of Congress.
✅ We helped drive the campaign to redesignate Nigeria a "Country of Particular Concern," laying the groundwork for real sanctions and accountability.
✅ Our educational efforts helped fuel the 95% vote by Texas Republicans to prohibit Sharia law – and the launch of the Sharia-Free America Caucus, now 60 members strong across 25 states.
**388 million Christians** – _**one in every seven believers on earth** _ – **live under threat right now for the same faith you are free to practice openly this morning.**
That freedom is not a possession. _**It is a responsibility.** _

And if you're able, maximize your impact by joining the Defenders Guild with a monthly commitment:** _ ](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=19bb697786954a2db72fe900648e4245&_e=WzahAEu1eclIGTLsigQA8fFaUCAK5DuwC6Xmk_ClvmndiqQSGHfjyOuflDKd8EhPvVBn9gIKtRLwG2fXMqmRE8u27ZmnYkIGKfBOglpbBpVV7B_W4jNHJRAytp9A9jP9AC1zB-yC6gbVQRB6DDq2HXXc9vBCQSCs4Iwzy_sX2w9FE0x7pYr7YIvUc4nIFtNoPMv8jdD3Ke-yVLOfm8hB5hNpi5-UrO0EevJlniSvBD__mNShALHeDZPTi5zY67bO8XxHhB6QqlBYH_xWTrXC27ZJNlfhsnCmdHft-qOroVEzNdWxDCM-lbq6u0QRmp4Sorepv_NTbbx3GagLrlVgeW75lc9sQti5g0s1Gjqm1CIo4akzRbLIzP6IqIGLg77WWSbWnZ-pg7HkFbmHO2k6KwcfCmbQ3TldbZulbDicNYPbilYvJkn8RAgw9qtpOTeen4M072Pd4Ohe_MEMMl9ao1iYZHyaoo7Ckj_-SShPqndB3HSk31AQZNt2HPwQsiqcjkDSjUm4mGKjd2S5VLZxZ_7usNstFO94yS1tK7IrNAeHN2ZGCLwGXW8DL_RYS03P)

In China, Pastor Ezra Jin spent 266 days in prison for leading one of the country's largest underground churches. Eight of his fellow pastors are still behind bars. In North Korea, owning a Bible can cost you the rest of your life in a labor camp. Secretary of State Marco Rubio named the second: "Radical Islam isn't content with controlling a single region or establishing a small caliphate. Its ideology is revolutionary. It aims to grow, to dominate, and to exert control over more lands and more populations." That is the whole project of political Islam: placing religious power above every constitution, every court, and every conscience. There is no room left in it for religious liberty. No room for a man to read the Gospel and decide for himself that it is true. And if you want to know what that project does to a man who decides exactly that, consider Nissar Hussain. Nissar left Islam and gave his life to Jesus Christ. For that, he spent seventeen years being hunted. Not in Tehran. Not in Nigeria. In Bradford, England. His kneecap was shattered in an attack outside his own home. His car was set on fire. His children were taunted in the street as "infidels." His family lived under police protection for nearly a decade. Not one bishop of the Church of England stood with him. Nissar's "crime" carries a death sentence in eleven nations on this earth. Now look at what happens where this ideology governs without restraint. In Nigeria, more than 100,000 Christians have been massacred since 2009. 19,000 churches burned or destroyed. Five million men, women, and children driven from their homes. This is not history. It is now. Just before midnight on July 26, militants entered the village of Naridon and went house to house, shooting. Thirty Christians were killed. Eleven were children. The youngest was three years old. On August 1, thousands gathered for a single funeral Mass. Twenty-seven caskets. That is not a distant tragedy. That is the destination. And that ideology now has political sponsorship inside the United States – with a partner supplying it lawyers, funding, and votes. Start in Dearborn, Michigan. Pastor Lorenzo Sewell prayed at President Trump's inauguration. Today he says Christians there come to him quietly, from every corner of the city, with the same message: "I'm with you, but I'm afraid to say it." Afraid to say they follow Christ. In America. Sewell describes a city where the call to prayer is broadcast over loudspeakers, where the public schools certify that every ounce of meat served to children is prepared according to Islamic ritual law, and where his own wife's life was threatened – the man's name and address handed to police – and nothing happened. "Think about being in a Christian nation," he said, "being afraid to talk about Christ." Then look at our schools. At two of the top public high schools in Virginia, students filmed promotional videos for their Muslim student clubs showing classmates hooded, dragged away, and thrown into car trunks – weeks after the anniversary of the October 7th massacre. The district disciplined them. Congress opened an investigation. And then a national Islamic advocacy group hauled the school system into federal court, arguing that punishing the students was itself discrimination. The provocation comes from one side. The lawyers come from the other. Then look at New York City. The largest city in America is now run by a self-described Democratic Socialist who took his oath of office on the Quran – elected with six figures of help from a network of Islamist organizations, including one whose leaders have been tied to terror-financing investigations. It's why he can visit a mosque in the morning and march in an LGBTQ parade that afternoon. The socialists supply the political machine and the moral cover. The Islamists supply the ideology and the money. Neither could do this alone. Together, they are formidable. "If the world hates you, keep in mind that it hated me first." – John 15:18 Jesus told us this would come. He did not tell us to be silent about it. This is precisely why Save the Persecuted Christians exists. We guide a coalition of over 200 organizations fighting this battle on both fronts at once – because they are the same battle. ✅ We brought Nissar Hussain to America and put him before members of Congress. ✅ We helped drive the campaign to redesignate Nigeria a "Country of Particular Concern," laying the groundwork for real sanctions and accountability. ✅ Our educational efforts helped fuel the 95% vote by Texas Republicans to prohibit Sharia law – and the launch of the Sharia-Free America Caucus, now 60 members strong across 25 states. 388 million Christians – one in every seven believers on earth – live under threat right now for the same faith you are free to practice openly this morning. That freedom is not a possession. It is a responsibility. | "DEFEND THE FAITH" Thank you for standing with those in need. In His name, Save the Persecuted Christians | | | | | | | | | | Save the Persecuted Christians PO Box 543 Monument, CO 80132 USA

By this month, Democrats will have 30 field offices open across Georgia, 60 full-time field organizers, and more than 100 coordinated campaign staff on the ground.
**It's the largest Democratic field operation ever assembled this early in Georgia.**
**_That didn't happen by accident._**
It happened because thousands of people stepped up with a dollar here, $5 there, and whatever they could afford to invest in this campaign.
**_You built this._**
You helped us hire organizers, open offices, and begin reaching voters months before ballots are cast. That's exactly how we win tough races in Georgia—not by waiting until the last minute, but by organizing early and everywhere. We were only able to do this because of your support.
_Meanwhile, Rick Jackson is spending $87 million on television ads. We can't and won't compete with that kind of personal fortune—but we can build the strongest grassroots campaign Georgia has ever seen._
**Launching the biggest field operation we've ever had took resources.** Keeping organizers in the field, opening offices, reaching voters, and **_growing this operation through Election Day requires more resources every single week._**

subject: Three months later, here's where we stand.
body:
|
# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138529261/644332905/-810700128?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3ODciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZDRhM2NkZGQtZTJhNy1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=tOds0oiRI0g3o0vzb-rVcZZ47kO-OUJ-KKbXwn4BSJw=)
Thank you. August is behind us — and thanks to your support, we closed the fundraising month strong. I don't take that for granted for a single day. It's been three months since the hazardous chemical incident at GKN Aerospace in Garden Grove sent shockwaves through our community. Over 5,000 small businesses were impacted. Families were evacuated. And amid the chaos, many were left without answers. So we got to work. I introduced the Hazardous Materials Transparency Act — legislation that requires facilities like GKN to notify communities in an emergency. I secured a Federal Emergency Declaration to deploy public health resources on the ground. And I worked with the Small Business Administration to secure a Disaster Declaration that unlocked low-interest recovery loans for impacted businesses and nonprofits. Last week I visited Sabroso! clean_body: | = Thank you. August is behind us — and thanks to your support, we closed the fundraising month strong. I don't take that for granted for a single day. It's been three months since the hazardous chemical incident at GKN Aerospace in Garden Grove sent shockwaves through our community. Over 5,000 small businesses were impacted. Families were evacuated. And amid the chaos, many were left without answers. So we got to work. I introduced the Hazardous Materials Transparency Act — legislation that requires facilities like GKN to notify communities in an emergency. I secured a Federal Emergency Declaration to deploy public health resources on the ground. And I worked with the Small Business Administration to secure a Disaster Declaration that unlocked low-interest recovery loans for impacted businesses and nonprofits. Last week I visited Sabroso! Mexican Kitchen in Garden Grove — one of the businesses hit hardest by the incident. I cooked with the chefs, talked with the owners, and sat down with KABC to talk about what we're doing to make sure this never happens to our community again. = | = There's a lot of noise in Washington, but this is exactly the type of work I ran for Congress to do. To show up, deliver, and make sure our community knows they have someone fighting for them in Congress. Thank you for believing in me enough to make it possible. subject: Terrible timing
body:
Derek, I have to be honest with you.
---
| [](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-el-sayed-split?amount=20&refcode=em_20260903_8938_fr&refcode2=8938_22930333_2kMsto&akid=8938%2E22930333%2E2kMsto)
---
Derek, I have to be honest with you.
The reality of having an August primary election date is not great. It’s pretty terrible timing for a campaign powered 100% by people like you.
Let me explain.
For the past few months, we’ve been running ads, making tight budget decisions, and relying on members of our grassroots team to power us through the final stretch of the primary campaign.
We were facing tens of millions in outside spending against us. We couldn’t afford to play it safe. **So, to put it bluntly, we practically drained our bank account leading up to August 4th.**
We made it through the primary, but that’s only _half_ the battle.
**The general election is here, and Mike Rogers has $51 million backing him to blanket the airwaves with misleading attack ads.**
It sounds daunting, but I’ve counted on this team before, and you’ve never let me down. I’m hoping I can count on you again today, Derek. body:

that person is."

Dear Patriot,

I stood on a porch in Detroit last week and showed a woman a
photograph of her own absentee ballot return envelope from the 2020
election. She looked at the signature and said, "THAT'S ME RIGHT
THERE."

THEN I SHOWED HER A SECOND ENVELOPE
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.
issued to the same voter, at the same address, for the same election.

She looked at it for a moment and said: "THAT'S NOT ME. I DON'T KNOW
WHO THAT PERSON IS."
[Donation Page]
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.
Here is the part I cannot get out of my head. She told us the City of
Detroit had already contacted her about that ballot back in 2020,
specifically because the signature did not match the one they had on
file for her. THE CITY ALREADY KNEW ABOUT THE DISCREPANCY, AND THAT
ENVELOPE WAS STILL RECEIVED, STILL STAMPED, AND NEVER REJECTED.

HELP ME FIND OUT WHO SIGNED IT.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

We did not obtain that document from a leak, a whistleblower, or a
lucky break, but the slow way instead, and the slow way is exactly the
reason almost nobody in America does this particular kind of work.

It took our team THREE TO FOUR YEARS OF FREEDOM OF INFORMATION ACT
REQUESTS to pry these certified records out of the City of Detroit Law
Department. That produced millions of pages, which my investigators
went through by hand, the analog way, one envelope at a time, because
the system is layered and complicated enough that hardly anyone ever
reaches the end of it.

FUND THE INVESTIGATION — CHIP IN $35 NOW
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.
Here is what turned up: DUPLICATE ABSENTEE BALLOT RETURN ENVELOPES
ISSUED TO THE SAME REGISTERED VOTERS. We scanned the barcodes on those
envelopes and found that the voter identification numbers matched
perfectly, while the ballot numbers did not. On several of them, the
two signatures look nothing alike, with one envelope signed in careful
cursive and the other in an illegible scrawl.

So we did the thing that almost nobody in journalism bothers to do
anymore, which is that WE WENT AND KNOCKED ON THE DOORS.

One of those addresses turned out to be a burned out, abandoned
building on Greenfield Road, where the local police confirmed that
nobody has lived for years and the flooring was not safe enough to
stand on. SOMEBODY IS STILL REGISTERED TO VOTE AT THAT ADDRESS, AND
THE RECORDS SHOW THAT PERSON CAST A BALLOT IN 2020 AND AGAIN IN 2024.

At another door, a man looked down at two envelopes with his own name
signed on both of them and said, "THAT'S ILLEGAL, MAN." Then he asked
me if we could scrape one of them off.

A woman threatened to put her dog on me, and another man ordered us
off his property, so we left. When our security guard could not
determine whether a pit bull in the next yard was actually chained up,
HE WALKED TOWARD THE ANIMAL TO FIND OUT, SO THAT NOBODY ELSE HAD TO.

That is the job, and that is precisely what your money pays for. KEEP
US ON THOSE DOORS — GIVE $35, $50 OR $100.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

SPONSOR A VOLUNTEER JOURNALIST — DONATE NOW
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.
Now let me tell you what I am _NOT_ saying, because this matters to
me.

I am not telling you that these envelopes prove two ballots were
actually counted, because they do not. Some of these voters may simply
have been mailed two envelopes by mistake and signed both of them
without thinking twice, and one woman told us exactly that. We say so
out loud, on camera, in the report itself.

What I _AM_ telling you is that these are CERTIFIED PUBLIC RECORDS,
and the questions they raise deserve a real answer. So we have now
filed a new request for the complete voter file, transaction history
and audit history for every person in this investigation.

We never ask you to accept a theory or to trust a narrative, because
we would rather SHOW YOU THE DOCUMENTS AND LET YOU DECIDE FOR
YOURSELF. That discipline is the only reason this organization has
survived everything people have thrown at it.

Here is why I need you today rather than next month.

AMERICA STARTS VOTING ON SEPTEMBER 19, the day the first ballots go
out - LESS THAN THREE WEEKS AWAY. The envelopes we are still reading
right now are from the 2020 election, and I would rather not spend
another four years filing paperwork to learn what happened in this
one.

That is the entire idea behind sponsoring a volunteer journalist:
TRAINED EYES INSIDE THE ROOM WHILE IT IS ACTUALLY HAPPENING, instead
of a records fight six years afterward.

You cannot personally spend four years reading envelopes in a Detroit
records office, but you can SPONSOR SOMEONE WHO WILL.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

You fund the mission, my team takes the risks, and you and your family
see the results with your own eyes. ARE YOU IN?
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

Thank you for all that you do, and please . . . stay tuned.

In Truth,[James O'Keefe]
James O'Keefe
Founder, O'Keefe Media Group

THE CITY ALREADY KNEW ABOUT THE DISCREPANCY, AND THAT ENVELOPE WAS STILL RECEIVED, STILL STAMPED, AND NEVER REJECTED. HELP ME FIND OUT WHO SIGNED IT. [ We did not obtain that document from a leak, a whistleblower, or a lucky break, but the slow way instead, and the slow way is exactly the reason almost nobody in America does this particular kind of work. It took our team THREE TO FOUR YEARS OF FREEDOM OF INFORMATION ACT REQUESTS to pry these certified records out of the City of Detroit Law Department. That produced millions of pages, which my investigators went through by hand, the analog way, one envelope at a time, because the system is layered and complicated enough that hardly anyone ever reaches the end of it. FUND THE INVESTIGATION — CHIP IN $35 NOW [ Here is what turned up: DUPLICATE ABSENTEE BALLOT RETURN ENVELOPES ISSUED TO THE SAME REGISTERED VOTERS. We scanned the barcodes on those envelopes and found that the voter identification numbers matched perfectly, while the ballot numbers did not. On several of them, the two signatures look nothing alike, with one envelope signed in careful cursive and the other in an illegible scrawl. So we did the thing that almost nobody in journalism bothers to do anymore, which is that WE WENT AND KNOCKED ON THE DOORS. One of those addresses turned out to be a burned out, abandoned building on Greenfield Road, where the local police confirmed that nobody has lived for years and the flooring was not safe enough to stand on. SOMEBODY IS STILL REGISTERED TO VOTE AT THAT ADDRESS, AND THE RECORDS SHOW THAT PERSON CAST A BALLOT IN 2020 AND AGAIN IN 2024. At another door, a man looked down at two envelopes with his own name signed on both of them and said, "THAT'S ILLEGAL, MAN." Then he asked me if we could scrape one of them off. A woman threatened to put her dog on me, and another man ordered us off his property, so we left. When our security guard could not determine whether a pit bull in the next yard was actually chained up, HE WALKED TOWARD THE ANIMAL TO FIND OUT, SO THAT NOBODY ELSE HAD TO. That is the job, and that is precisely what your money pays for. KEEP US ON THOSE DOORS — GIVE $35, $50 OR $100. [ SPONSOR A VOLUNTEER JOURNALIST — DONATE NOW [ Now let me tell you what I am NOT saying, because this matters to me. I am not telling you that these envelopes prove two ballots were actually counted, because they do not. Some of these voters may simply have been mailed two envelopes by mistake and signed both of them without thinking twice, and one woman told us exactly that. We say so out loud, on camera, in the report itself. What I AM telling you is that these are CERTIFIED PUBLIC RECORDS, and the questions they raise deserve a real answer. So we have now filed a new request for the complete voter file, transaction history and audit history for every person in this investigation. We never ask you to accept a theory or to trust a narrative, because we would rather SHOW YOU THE DOCUMENTS AND LET YOU DECIDE FOR YOURSELF. That discipline is the only reason this organization has survived everything people have thrown at it. Here is why I need you today rather than next month. AMERICA STARTS VOTING ON SEPTEMBER 19, the day the first ballots go out - LESS THAN THREE WEEKS AWAY. The envelopes we are still reading right now are from the 2020 election, and I would rather not spend another four years filing paperwork to learn what happened in this one. That is the entire idea behind sponsoring a volunteer journalist: TRAINED EYES INSIDE THE ROOM WHILE IT IS ACTUALLY HAPPENING, instead of a records fight six years afterward. You cannot personally spend four years reading envelopes in a Detroit records office, but you can SPONSOR SOMEONE WHO WILL. [ You fund the mission, my team takes the risks, and you and your family see the results with your own eyes. ARE YOU IN? [ Thank you for all that you do, and please . . . stay tuned. In Truth,[James O'Keefe] James O'Keefe Founder, O'Keefe Media Group P.S. A man looked at his own name signed on two different ballot envelopes and asked me if we could scrape one of them off. That is where this country is right now, and the only thing that changes it is somebody who keeps showing up at the door with a camera and a stack of certified public records. A $10 billion contract awarded to M1 Support Services for U.S. Army helicopter pilot training is raising alarms over a potential conflict of interest involving Deputy Secretary of War Steve Feinberg. The company that won one of the Army's largest training deals in history is controlled by the investment firm Feinberg co-founded and ran for more than three decades.
LOOMER UNLEASHED is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..NzsGQ0qiP9tCOGj-WxNWN0Vi8NDpls9Mc_0v0i7aHDI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=214079321)
M1, which has been controlled by Cerberus Capital Management since 2024, will provide Initial Entry Rotary Wing training under the Army's Flight School Next program for up to 26 years, running through August 2052. The firm will supply the aircraft, instructors, maintenance, and simulators at Fort Rucker, Alabama, while the Army retains oversight of training standards and safety.
The Department of War selected M1 from 11 competing bids for the $10 billion contract. M1 celebrated the win in a press release, which you can read [here](https://substack.com/redirect/95bf19dd-134c-45b6-9796-b9bf23e1f9c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/76649a82-440e-4c8a-b7de-38aca575c8f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
On May 28, 2024, Cerberus Capital Management acquired a controlling interest in M1 Support Services, a Texas-based provider of military aircraft maintenance, logistics, and flight training to the U.S. government. Barely two years later, that investment has paid off with M1 landing a multi-decade contract worth up to $10 billion, a massive sum.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..NzsGQ0qiP9tCOGj-WxNWN0Vi8NDpls9Mc_0v0i7aHDI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=214079321)
Cerberus was co-founded by Steve Feinberg, who built the firm into a global investment giant with approximately $70 billion in assets and steered it aggressively into U.S. defense sector investments. Feinberg left his role as co-CEO of Cerberus when he was [sworn in as Deputy Secretary of War in March 2025.](https://substack.com/redirect/743ba666-d58b-4d42-a227-f60db13f1f83?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Feinberg formally divested from the firm upon entering government, but he retained a financial relationship with Cerberus, according to ethics filings.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c042632e-bfa2-4ec3-829e-825d2c581034?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The $10 billion award places a company tied to the Pentagon's second-ranking civilian official at the center of one of the Army's largest multi-decade training contracts. The arrangement creates a clear appearance of a conflict of interest, especially given Feinberg's senior position at the Pentagon in a department that oversees acquisitions and the contracting process.
The deal's extraordinary length, a contract running through August 2052, extends well beyond typical political tenures, and will be active after Feinberg has left the Pentagon.
Ethics rules and recusal procedures at the Department of War are designed to prevent exactly these types of issues. Yet the scale and timing of the award are highly suspect.
It's important that all officials in the Trump administration conduct themselves with the utmost ethical standards in mind at all times, because their behavior will be used against President Trump if and when the Democrats take back control of the House and Senate this November. Every appearance of self-dealing, however it may ultimately be explained, is a gift-wrapped talking point for Democrat oversight committees waiting to weaponize it.
The American people deserve to know whether or not a $10 billion, 26-year commitment of their tax dollars was awarded based on merit, or a personal relationship.

name: Francesca Governali, LCV
subject: TAKE ACTION: Hands Off Our National Forests!
body:
Add your name before September 21!

If you are unable to see the message below, [click here to view](https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTM5MzMyMzMS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjU0MDAyNDM2NAS2&mt=1&rt=0).
| | | |
---
| | | |
## _**OUR FORESTS ARE UNDER ATTACK:**_
**STOP Trump’s Repeal of the Roadless Rule!**
The Trump administration has officially proposed repealing protections for more than **44 MILLION ACRES of our national forests**. If this succeeds, it would mean more logging, more roads through undeveloped wilderness, and the destruction of remote, ecologically intact forests that are essential to the health and safety of people, wildlife, and our climate. **_Comments are open until September 21._** The administration needs to hear us loud and clear: Hands Off Our National Forests!
[**_Add your name to defend our forests >>_**](https://links.messages.lcv.)
---
| | | [ADD YOUR NAME](https://links.messages.lcv.)
---
| | The Trump administration has officially proposed repealing the Roadless Rule, which protects more than **44 MILLION acres of land from logging and road construction, including old-growth forests** like the Tongass National Forest in Alaska.
---
| | The Roadless Rule is one of the most important safeguards we have to protect our forests from corporate development. For the last 25 years, the Roadless Rule has protected America’s most ecologically intact forests and wild places. Now, in a clear giveaway to billionaire industry executives — and against the wishes of the millions of people who have voiced their support for these protections over the last three decades — Trump and his allies want to gut these protections.
---
| | This rollback would jeopardize our nation’s most treasured old-growth forests and threaten the health and safety of communities across the country — all for corporate polluter profits.
---
| | [**_We can’t let corporate polluters tear down our irreplaceable old-growth forests, Peter. Add your name to keep our forests protected >>_**](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/8wqzCjp~)
---
| | | [TAKE ACTION NOW](https://links.messages.lcv.)
---
| | This rollback is a blatant, reckless giveaway to Big Polluters — with devastating costs for our communities and our planet:
* **Wildlife habitat will be shattered** , pushing vulnerable species to the brink.
* **Drinking water will be polluted for millions of Americans** , due to increased runoff and contamination from deforestation.
* **Old-growth forests will be destroyed** , releasing more carbon and worsening the climate crisis.

body:
Please keep your faith in me.
| | | | [](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
---
Blind faith in something is never easy.

But in 2016, that’s all my campaign had.

I was an unproven, untested political outsider running for the highest office in the land: The President of the United States.

**Everywhere around me were those who couldn’t wait to see me fail.
**
But also, there were my supporters.

**Patriots like YOU who risked everything to believe in me.
**
And with your support, we achieved the impossible.

Ten years ago, I could never have imagined where I would be today.
**That’s why it is my greatest honor, every day, to be your President. I will never forget the trust you have bestowed upon me.** ****

[](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
So today, I’m reaching out to you to make a promise, a solemn vow to the supporters that have been with me since the beginning.
Right now, as you read this, the Radical Left is working overtime to dismantle the movement that we have built together, destroy our great country, and halt the Golden Age we began just two years ago.
**They will stop at nothing to destroy what we have built. We cannot let them.**
I promise to YOU, the American People, hand over heart:
**_That I will NEVER surrender. I will never give up, and I will never stop fighting to Make America Great Again._**
Because here is the truth the Radical Left is trying so desperately to hide:

**[We have never been closer to Making America Great Again.](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)**
I know the pressure is heavy right now.

But please, please keep your faith in our fight.

**The most pivotal election of our lifetime is right around the corner. The Radical Left are celebrating just thinking about the chance to dismantle the MAGA movement if they win.**

If they succeed, everything we have accomplished in the last two years will be swept away overnight.

We CANNOT let that happen.

**[Please, if you are financially able, can I count on your support for just $26? Your contribution today could be the deciding factor in determining MAGA’s future.](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)** **[]()**
I’m asking you today with a humble heart; please keep your faith in me, our country, and the movement we have built together.

[DONATE $26](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
THANK YOU & GOD BLESS

And I worked three jobs in college and medical school to fulfill my dream of becoming a doctor. **I’m not sharing this story to earn sympathy points. I’m sharing it because these experiences shaped who I am and how I fight.** They're why I'll never look the other way while Ohio families struggle to afford groceries, healthcare, childcare, or a place to call home. I know what it's like to need someone to fight for you. **That’s why I’m running for governor.** Look, there’s no doubt this will be a tough fight. clean_body: I was 12 years old, homeless, and living in a tent. | | | | I think it was somewhere off Route 7. I was 12 years old, homeless, and living in a tent. It wasn't easy, but it made me tough. Derek, by the time I was in middle school, I had been a frequent flier with children’s services. I had lived in over a dozen homes and experienced abuse, hunger, and homelessness. But I was determined to find a way out. I credit public schools with saving my life. And I worked three jobs in college and medical school to fulfill my dream of becoming a doctor. I’m not sharing this story to earn sympathy points. I’m sharing it because these experiences shaped who I am and how I fight. They're why I'll never look the other way while Ohio families struggle to afford groceries, healthcare, childcare, or a place to call home. I know what it's like to need someone to fight for you. That’s why I’m running for governor. Look, there’s no doubt this will be a tough fight. I’m up against an out-of-touch billionaire who has no idea what it’s like to struggle. He’s spending tens of millions to buy this state for his own selfish gain. But I’m ready for a tough fight. And if I learned anything from my childhood, it's that no one gets through anything alone. 🌨️ SUPER EL NIÑO IS HERE — BUT THERE’S A CATCHThe good news: The equatorial Pacific is warming dramatically and El Niño conditions are already in place. That normally favors the kind of southern storm track New Mexico desperately needs.
Mark’s early prediction?
👉 Northern New Mexico snowpack around 110% of average.After two brutal La Niña winters, that could feel VERY wet. But there’s one thing keeping him from predicting a blockbuster winter.
Ocean temperatures off the West Coast are considerably cooler than they were during the massive 1997–98 El Niño. That colder pattern — called the Pacific Decadal Oscillation — could interfere with some of the effects we normally expect from a strong El Niño.
So Mark brought back an old favorite from his KRQE days: The Bust Potential.His number right now: 35%. That means he sees roughly a 65% chance that this El Niño delivers a pretty good winter for New Mexico.
And if you're wondering whether to book the ski trip? Mark says YES.Taos. Red River. Angel Fire. Ski Santa Fe. Telluride. Wolf Creek.He especially likes the potential for the earlier part of the season.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/1AZijzmQY2B?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |

🚨 65% OF NEW MEXICANS SAY NOThe data-center fight in New Mexico isn't going away. A new Albuquerque Journal poll found:
• 65% oppose large-scale data center development
• Only 20% support it
• A majority of Republicans, Democrats AND independents oppose new data centers
Those numbers are extraordinary. But we think there’s a much bigger conversation New Mexico needs to have. People have legitimate concerns about electricity rates and water — especially when we're literally walking through a dry Rio Grande. Those questions MUST be answered.
But Mark argues that simply saying “no data centers” isn't a realistic answer either. Artificial intelligence is quickly becoming a major global economic and national-security competition, and China would be more than happy to watch America decide not to build the infrastructure necessary to compete.
So where’s the balance?Data centers need to prove — with actual numbers, not talking points — that they won't raise electricity costs for New Mexico families or threaten our limited water resources. Until they do, this opposition isn't going anywhere.
🗳️ THE POLLING IS ROUGH — BUT THERE'S A CATCHWe also dig into the latest New Mexico statewide polling. Right now, several Republican candidates have significant ground to make up.
Ben Ray Luján leads Republican Larry Marker by 15 points in the U.S. Senate race, while Democrats also hold leads in several other statewide contests. We explain why money, name recognition and independent voters matter so much in these races — and why saying “polls don't matter” isn't particularly helpful.
Polls are snapshots.
The question is what campaigns DO with the information. And nationally, there's another fascinating possibility developing. If the polls are underestimating Republicans by just 2–4 points — something we've seen happen before — the Senate map looks VERY different. Michigan could flip. Texas, Iowa, Ohio and Maine could stay Republican.
And suddenly you could be looking at a 53–47 Republican Senate.
Spoiler alert: Mark isn't quite ready to guarantee it.Krysty is feeling considerably more optimistic. 😂
🏛️ FINALLY, SOMETHING AMERICA AGREES ONRepublicans and Democrats have found common ground!Unfortunately, it's this: 89% of Americans now believe corruption in the federal government is widespread.Democrats: 91%Republicans: 83%Independents: 90%
But the really fascinating part is how those numbers have changed depending on who's occupying the White House.
We break down what the numbers reveal — and why government accountability shouldn't depend on which political party happens to be in charge.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/metiTfe20XG?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |

🚙 AND THEN THERE'S THE $208,000 RANGE ROVER...Yes.$208,000!For an electric Range Rover. Krysty loves how they look.Mark loves reminding her how often Range Rover owners allegedly end up visiting the mechanic.This conversation goes exactly where you'd expect. 😂

| | Dear Peter,
**I will be visiting the Israeli-occupied West Bank later this month, thanks to the incredible efforts of activists and organizers on the ground in the West Bank and the International Federation for Rights and Development in Europe.**
I will be talking to Palestinians and Palestinian Americans about the holocaust being carried out by the Israeli state and the brutality of the decades of occupation. Our goal will be to help further expose the horrors taking place on Palestinian lands. I will also be visiting Palestinian children in Egypt and Turkey, all of whom are sole survivors of their families and have suffered untold atrocities. All of these children have personally faced Israeli bombardment and have had to undergo limb amputations.
The Israeli state, empowered by U.S. imperialism and war-profiteering billionaires and multimillionaires, has continued the genocide in Gaza for well over a thousand days. At the same time, violence against Palestinians in the West Bank has dramatically escalated, both directly from the Israeli state forces and from state-sanctioned, right-wing settlers. In total, since the genocide began, Israel has killed over a thousand people in the West Bank and inflicted incalculable damage on Palestinian homes and farms.
**Nothing short of smashing the apartheid state of Israel will end the indescribable suffering of the Palestinian people.**
For that, working-class militant movements in the United States will be crucial because Israel exists as a garrison state for the economic and geopolitical interests of the American capitalist class and other imperialist powers.
This also means that it is a fool’s errand to place any faith in either the Democratic Party or Republican Party, as both are parties of the war-profiteering billionaires and multimillionaires. The strategy of the leadership of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) of supporting careerist Democratic Party politicians is a complete dead end for the Palestinian cause.
**Anything other than leadership to build an antiwar movement that unambiguously fights against both the Democratic and Republican parties will lead to further betrayals of the Palestinian people.**
Solidarity,
Kshama Sawant

name: Darline Graham
subject: Look at California before you look away from this
body:
While Gavin Newsom tours South Carolina, take a look at what he actually did to his own state. |
---

**Peter - Gavin Newsom is in South Carolina right now.**

He's holding meet-and-greets and rallying support for Democrats up and down the ballot. Democrats brought him in on purpose. They want to turn South Carolina into California, and I'm not going to let that happen.

_Before anybody in this state takes a single thing Gavin Newsom says seriously, I want you to look at what he actually did with the power he was given._

As Governor, he ran California into the ground. Businesses are fleeing the state, homelessness has gotten worse, and gas prices and the cost of living have pushed working families out of their own communities. That is not a talking point. That is what happened under his leadership, in the state he still runs today.

_Now he's building the same kind of Democratic machine here._

Annie Andrews has already raised nearly $11 million, much of it from the same national donor network Newsom is rallying here. Every stop he makes on this trip helps energize the exact coalition trying to elect someone who will vote with Chuck Schumer, not South Carolina.

clean_body: While Gavin Newsom tours South Carolina, take a look at what he actually did to his own state. | Peter - Gavin Newsom is in South Carolina right now. He's holding meet-and-greets and rallying support for Democrats up and down the ballot. Democrats brought him in on purpose. They want to turn South Carolina into California, and I'm not going to let that happen. Before anybody in this state takes a single thing Gavin Newsom says seriously, I want you to look at what he actually did with the power he was given. As Governor, he ran California into the ground. Businesses are fleeing the state, homelessness has gotten worse, and gas prices and the cost of living have pushed working families out of their own communities. That is not a talking point. That is what happened under his leadership, in the state he still runs today. Now he's building the same kind of Democratic machine here. Annie Andrews has already raised nearly $11 million, much of it from the same national donor network Newsom is rallying here. Every stop he makes on this trip helps energize the exact coalition trying to elect someone who will vote with Chuck Schumer, not South Carolina. I did not spend thirty years serving South Carolina to watch it get handed over to the same failed ideas that wrecked California. Peter, I need your help to keep California money and ideas out of our state today. Please don't let Gavin Newsom's failed record become South Carolina's future. Thank you for standing with me, Darline Graham P.S. body:
Hello - My name is Mary Peltola, and after winning the primary, I am officially running in the general election for United States Senate in Alaska. I want to share with you why I made the decision to run – and to ask for your support as we begin the general election together. But if you already understand how important this race and your support are, and you’re ready to join our fight for fish, family, and freedom, please use this button to split a contribution between my campaign for U.S. Senate and John Hickenlooper: | | [CONTRIBUTE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138532781/644343376/1260721273?refcode=email_090326_peltola&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlNjZlZjFiZS1lZWE3LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=MCOHUbH5pJzvTit1fRB6aBuhFNxkmm-jwb6Ua39a8_o=)
---
Now here’s a bit more on how I came to this decision.
When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance.
Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity.
Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find.
So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families.
And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying nearly 20 bucks for a gallon of fuel. They don’t even believe us.
They're focused on their own wallets – not ours.
And when they actually work together on something, it’s usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest.
It’s why our prices keep rising, all while the healthcare and services Alaskans rely on get gutted.
I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home.
My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning.
But if we’re going to secure Alaska’s future, we need another priority: fighting corruption.
I'm running for Alaska's Senate seat because it is the fight for our future.
**This is going to be the closest and most consequential Senate race this year, and I cannot do this alone. There is only one way we’ll be able to flip this seat... and that is together.**
So I am asking:
[Please split a contribution between John Hickenlooper and my campaign for the U.S. Senate today. We are looking for a huge surge in support to get our general election campaign off to a strong start and put us in a position to win. No donation is too small. This is one of them. **This week, I authorized our campaign to begin placing a new major television ad, even though we haven't finished raising the money to cover the full buy.** I don't love taking that kind of financial risk. Rick Jackson is betting that if he spends enough money, he can hide the fact that he got rich by profiting off our health care. He wants to hide the fact that he promised to be “Trump’s favorite Governor,” and that there’s not a single thing he disagrees with Trump on. He's betting that an $87 million wall of television ads will drown out every volunteer, every organizer, every small-dollar donor, and every conversation about what's really at stake in this election. **I'm betting he's wrong.** But only if we have the resources to fight back. That's why I instructed my team to start locking in our own TV reservations. Every day we wait, ad inventory becomes more expensive, more limited, and more valuable. If we're going to compete, we have to claim our place on the air now—not months from now. It's a big commitment for a grassroots campaign. But this campaign has never been built on billionaire checks. It's been built by people giving what they can because they believe Georgia deserves a governor who will fight for working families—not another wealthy executive trying to buy public office. Rick Jackson may have $87 million reserved. We have each other. Midterm races are decided by turnout margins that would look like rounding errors in a presidential race. Aparade of newly trained Puntland Security Forces soldiers, trained to combat ISIS, in the Bari region of Puntland, January 30, 2025. Photo: REUTERS/Feisal Omar
MOGADISHU, Somalia --On September 3, shortly after sunset, U.S. surveillance drones began carrying out reconnaissance missions in two areas of the Al-Miskad mountains in Puntland, Somalia, according to Puntland security officials that spoke with Drop Site. The two localities--Togga Miraale and Togga Baalade--are considered strongholds for ISIS militants by local authorities.
During the mission, the drones spotted alleged ISIS militants traveling with a donkey cart in the locality of Togga Baalade, the security officials said, and began carrying out airstrikes nearby at around 8:30 p.m. The strikes, which were accompanied by more drone surveillance missions further northwest in the Sanaag region, broke a relative lull in U.S. attacks in Somalia, justified as a means of bolstering local government forces against ISIS and Al-Shabaab militants.
AFRICOM did not respond to a request for comment, but Puntland security officials told Drop Site they expect the U.S. air campaign in Somalia only to intensify in the foreseeable future. Key to that expanded effort is the development of a new U.S. military base in the port city of Bosaso announced last month. Though the officials argue that U.S. air support is necessary for the war against ISIS in Somalia, U.S. operations have been blamed for killing and displacing thousands of civilians.
Bosaso straddles the northern Somali coast on the shores of the Gulf of Aden. Home to around 1 million people, it is also known as a major route for human trafficking and refugee flows, with East African migrants crossing the Gulf of Aden in a bid to reach Yemen and the Arab world.
